jobs.title: Circularity Specialist
jobs.description:
As a Circularity Specialist at Avery Dennison, you will serve as a core technical expert and enterprise catalyst within the global Circularity & Waste Center of Expertise. In this high-impact, global role, you will drive portfolio readiness roadmaps across circularity pathways—specifically focusing on the recyclability, reusability, and compostability of packaging and materials across all Avery Dennison business units. This position bridges deep technical engineering with enterprise-wide leadership, translating complex environmental science, packaging trade dynamics, and global regulatory mandates into clear commercial strategies.

Key Responsibilities

Employees work in a hybrid mode at our Mentor, OH facility.

• Deep Technical Circularity Leadership: Serve as the enterprise subject matter expert on material technicalities across recycling (mechanical & chemical), reuse models, and compostability (bio-based and compostable packaging formats), conducting detailed technical evaluations on product recyclability and circular design.
• Enterprise Collaboration & Influence: Partner across global business units to translate complex circularity challenges into actionable commercial opportunities and present technical positions to senior business unit leaders and multi-disciplinary teams.
• External Advocacy & Standards Setting: Actively participate and sit on key industry committees, trade associations, and standards organizations to advocate for progressive, harmonized global circularity standards.
• Regulatory Readiness & Roadmap Execution: Build and execute global readiness roadmaps to navigate complex evolving legislation, including Extended Producer Responsibility (EPR), Packaging and Packaging Waste Regulation (PPWR), PCR minimum content mandates, and Truth-in-Labeling laws.
• Global Market Intelligence: Monitor global circularity pathways, tracking PCR feedstock supply chains, bio-derived innovations, and textile/apparel circularity frameworks to keep the enterprise ahead of market shifts.

• Experience: 5–7 years of hands-on experience in corporate sustainability, packaging engineering, material science, or technical sustainability consulting.
• Education: Bachelor’s degree in Packaging Engineering, Materials Science, Environmental Sciences, Sustainability, or a related technical field (Master’s degree preferred).

Preferred / Nice-to-Have Skills:

• Functional knowledge of textile and apparel circularity and end-of-life pathways (distinct from traditional packaging).
• Active engagement or leadership history on industry trade association technical committees.
• Technical Depth: Proven technical capability in Design for Recycling (DfR), circular packaging design, compostability standards, and end-of-life recovery systems across global markets.
• Communication & Executive Presence: Demonstrated ability to simplify complex technical topics for diverse business audiences and influence decision-makers across matrixed, cross-functional global business units.
• Regulatory Acumen: Working knowledge of current and emerging global environmental regulations impacting packaging and labeling (e.g., EU PPWR, global EPR schemes, FTC Green Guides / Truth in Labeling).

Pay Transparency:

The salary range for this position is $73,575 -109,872/ year. The hiring base salary range above represents what Avery Dennison reasonably expects to pay for this position as of the date of this posting. Actual salaries will vary within the range, and in some circumstances may be above or below the range, based on various factors including but not limited to a candidate’s relevant skills, experience, education and training, and location, as well as the job scope and complexity, responsibilities, and regular and/or necessary travel required for the position, which may change depending on the candidate pool. Upon completion of the program and certification, if no ASM or otherwise qualified role is available AND the ST is meeting performance standards, the employee may remain in the ST role up to 12-months OR until an ASM or another qualified role is available (whichever comes first).

Once an ASM or another qualified role is available, the certified ST must interview for that available role.

If promotion to the role of ACCOUNT SALES MANAGER (or other role) does not happen prior to the expiration of the 12-mos completion period, the SALES TRAINEE role will be vacated due to end of assignment unless an exception applies.

For exception, based on continued high performance, no open roles and certification completion, a manager may extend the 12-month completion period an additional 6-months.

jobs.title: H&M Store Manager - Capital City Mall
jobs.description:
About the Role

As a Store Manager, you’ll be responsible for the total holistic omni customer experience in your store, ensuring high visual and commercial curation & standards according to the store format location and global & regional strategies. You have the responsibility of leading the full store team to excel. You create an inclusive culture that promotes collaboration and entrepreneurial spirit and are responsible & aware of the store’s strengths, opportunities, and competitors. You’ll also be the person who analyzes and follows up on sales, creating plans to optimize results and profits.

A Day in the Life

Working at H&M means no two days are ever the same, but a typical day will include the following responsibilities*

Customer Sales & Profit

• Responsible for the total OMNI customer experience in your store, ensuring visual and commercial curation according to your store format environment, global guidelines and regional strategies
• Represent yourself and the H&M brand positively during all customer interactions
• Establish, analyze, and follow up on sales & budget goals, and create plans to optimize results
• Ensure personal customer service is provided in all areas of the store, ensuring your team initiates customer interactions, guiding customers through fashion stories and works towards actively selling our products
• Following up that your teams are actively promoting our Customer Loyalty App (Hello Member) & in-store sustainability initiatives
• Schedule to budgeted hours plan in line with sales budget and commercial activities
• Ensure correct routines in fitting room and checkout, including transaction, returns and exchanges
• Be aware of your store strengths and opportunities, identifying commercial opportunities and acting on them. Maintain competitor awareness & knowledge
• Manage store maintenance in a cost-efficient way
• Ensure all admin routines for both people and operations are handled in a correct way

Fashion & Trend Awareness

• Keep up to date with fashion scene, trends, tendencies, styles, brands, products, competitors, and relevant influencers, etc
• Ensure your team provides product and fashion knowledge as well as other relevant information during customer interactions
• Ensure good understanding of the local area of your store, customers, competition, and fashion trends

Team & Development

• Responsible for talent and performance management in your store – recruiting, onboarding, upskilling, and developing your team
• Complete performance evaluations and succession planning to support business needs & team
• Retain and share your knowledge and skills with your team
• Strong collaboration with Area team and store leadership team including VMs
• Ensure excellent communication & professionalism
• Responsible for the teams planning & scheduling
• Regular communication to store colleagues to inform, motivate and inspire – daily/weekly meetings, etc
• Ensure all procedures, routines, security, and legal requirements in all areas of the store are followed
• Participate in relevant available Onboarding & introduction processes, trainings and courses relevant for your role & future development

Retail Operations/ Visual & Commercial Execution

• Ensure a clean and tidy sales floor and back of house.
• Ensure high fashion quality, visual and commercial product presentation, with great garment care.
• Ensure good stock levels and provide input on allocation to relevant area or sales market colleagues
• Responsible for & supports with the daily opening & closing of store routines and processes
• Ensure the full garment cycle – from delivery to garment presentation – and fitting room routines are according to our standards, processes, utilizing all tools and technology provided
• Upkeep & following best practices for any in-store OMNI Services & in-store tech services/tools etc (Instore Care App, Click & Collect, Smart Store etc)
• Secure a strong balance and the maintenance of price signs in-store and throughout the sales floor/store following guidelines according to global & local strategies & sales market/regional requirements to ensure a strong and consistent price perception throughout the store
• Update & maintenance of BOH areas for all colleagues (key information, health & safety, tidiness etc)

Who You Are

• To be a successful and effective Store Manager, you’ll be a strong leader who enjoys taking responsibility for others.
• Confident in team coaching & development. You must be ambitious, an effective communicator, an analytical solution finder, capable of working with numbers & managing statistics.
• Relevant experience working in a leadership position that you can apply to your role
• Retail management and retail operations experience
• Experience collaborating closely with a team

Why You’ll Love Working at H&M

• We value diverse backgrounds, including but not limited to race, ethnicity, gender, age, religion, sexual orientation, and disability
• We pride ourselves on being a values-driven organization, guided by our 7 unique values that have been part of our success story for over 75 years
• You’ll have access to our Colleague Resource Groups (CRGs) to find community and networking opportunities among colleagues
• We are an inclusive company where you’re encouraged to be yourself at work
• You will have access to a large global talent community, where career growth and aspirations have no limits
• We believe in supporting your overall wellbeing and offer comprehensive benefits inclusive of health insurance, wellness and family support programs, company match retirement plan, paid leave programs, and paid time off, including a community day to serve your local community
• You’ll be able to express your personal style with our employee discount at H&M, & Other Stories, and COS

Compensation: expected base salary range is $67,400 - $77,480 annually**

EEOC Code: OFM

Pay Status: Salary, Non-Exempt (Exempt for Top Volume locations)

*This job posting highlights the most critical responsibilities and requirements of the job and is not all-inclusive. There may be additional duties, and responsibilities assigned for this job at the company’s discretion.

**H&M, in good faith, has assessed this posted range of compensation as the accurate range for this role and location at the time of this posting. H&M may ultimately pay more or less than the posted range depending on candidate qualifications. This range may be modified in the future.

We are committed to providing reasonable accommodations for applicants with disabilities. If you require assistance or accommodation during the application or interview process, please contact us at https://hm.ethicspoint.com, and use Ask a Question.

Benefits:

We offer all our employees at H&M Group attractive benefits with extensive development opportunities around the globe. All our employees receive a staff discount card, usable on all our H&M Group brands in stores and online. Brands covered by the discount are H&M (Beauty and Move included), COS, Weekday, Monki, H&M HOME, & Other Stories, ARKET, Afound. In addition to our staff discount, all our employees are included in our H&M Incentive Program – HIP. You can read more about our H&M Incentive Program here.

In addition to our global benefits, all our local markets offer different competitive perks and benefits. Please note that they may differ between employment type and countries.

We offer: 25% Staff Discount - Medical, Pharmacy Vision and Dental Coverage – Employee Assistance Program - Vacation, Wellness, Holiday and Parental Pay – 401K – Commuter Benefits, Health and Dependent Care FSA. Plus, additional Voluntary Benefits.

Inclusion & Diversity:

H&M is a part of H&M Group. At H&M Group, we’re determined to create and maintain inclusive, diverse and equitable workplaces throughout our organisation. Our teams should consist of a variety of people that share and combine their knowledge, experience and ideas. Having a diverse workforce leads to a positive impact on how we address challenges, on what we perceive possible and on how we choose to relate to our colleagues and customers all over the world. Hence all diversity dimensions are taken into consideration in our recruitment process.

We strive to have a fair and equal process and therefore kindly ask you not to attach a cover letter in your application as they often contain information that easily can trigger unintentional biases.

Company Description:

At H&M, our purpose is to liberate fashion for the many. We want to shape a new world in Fashion. A world with one ultimate goal: to unleash your self-expression. As an H&M colleague, you’re encouraged to be yourself & more. You’ll take on new responsibilities from day one, learn skills for life, and find new ways to make your big dreams come true.

Our company is committed to fostering a culture of inclusion and belonging, and we actively seek colleagues who share our commitment.

To manage the high volume of applications for roles with leadership responsibilities, we use an online assessment method. You will need to complete it as part of the application and screening process. Your responses will be scored by an assessment tool that applies to predefined criteria set by H&M Group.

After completing the assessment, you’ll have the opportunity to share feedback and ask questions.

jobs.title: State Affairs Lead
jobs.description:
The State Affairs Manager is responsible for managing and implementing Syngenta’s legislative and regulatory priorities across the Midwest and Central U.S. This role engages with elected and appointed officials at the state level and builds strategic relationships with key commodity groups, industry associations, and other stakeholders to protect and advance Syngenta’s business interests while supporting sound, science-based regulatory policy.

The State Affairs Manager will collaborate across Syngenta business units, including Crop Protection, Seeds, and SBI Sales, as well as State and Federal Registration teams, on key initiatives and projects as directed by the State Affairs Team Leader.

Working closely with the Stewardship Team, this position will support product stewardship initiatives across assigned states. The State Affairs Manager will also oversee Syngenta contract lobbyists and consultants within the region and serve as a primary point of contact for state commodity groups and regional trade associations.

Additionally, this role serves as a key Syngenta representative with State Secretaries, Directors, and Commissioners of Agriculture, other state regulatory officials, and university leaders.

Employees may work remotely in Indiana, with travel throughout the assigned Midwest and Central U.S. region as business needs require.

Accountabilities

• Manage legislation in assigned states
• Enable Syngenta Freedom to Operate
• Coordinate initiatives with Key Commodity Groups, Agribusiness Associations, Farm Bureaus, and Farmer Unions at the state level
• Assist Sales, State Regulatory Affairs, and R&D with regulatory issues affecting Syngenta
• Develop a network of key contacts to promote Business Interests and Policy Priorities
• Develop and coordinate Syngenta comments on regulatory and legislative issues
• Direct contracted state lobbyists and consultants
• Support the Stewardship Team on water quality and other product stewardship projects

Essential Skills & Knowledge

• Strong science, regulatory, and policy expertise, coupled with a deep understanding of other agricultural stakeholders' perspectives
• Strong oral, presentation, and written communication skills
• Excellent at networking, both internally and externally; readily gains support from many teams within Syngenta as well as external influencers
• High energy, a "can-do" attitude, leads by example, and is results-oriented
• Ability to work independently and manage time effectively
• Adapts readily and effectively to changing priorities
• Strong project management, organizational, and leadership abilities to initiate, manage, control, and complete objectives efficiently and effectively
• Proven leadership, networking, and teamwork accomplishments
• Existing knowledge of key regulatory and political issues
• Previous Crop Protection, Seeds, Government Affairs, or R&D experience is preferred
• Successful track record of managing complex issues and influencing key stakeholders
• Strong interpersonal experience

• BS or BA in Agricultural/Life Sciences or Agri-Business with 4-8 years of experience
• Broad knowledge of agriculture and general farming practices
• Public speaking experience
• Knowledge of crop production systems, food supply chains, agricultural businesses and markets
• Knowledge of regulatory requirements for registration of pesticides and seed traits
• Experience with the political and regulatory process
• Working knowledge of the US regulatory environment and processes
• Strong writing skills

• All applicants must be eligible to work in the US without visa support
• Travel Requirement 30-50%
• This position will be based remotely, servicing the Midwest - Central US

What We Offer:

• A culture that celebrates belonging and collaboration, promotes professional development and strives for a work-life balance that supports the team members. Offers flexible work options to support your work and personal needs.
• Full Benefit Package (Medical, Dental & Vision) that starts your first day.
• 401k plan with company match, Profit Sharing & Retirement Savings Contribution.
• Paid Vacation, Paid Holidays, Maternity and Paternity Leave, Education Assistance, Wellness Programs, Corporate Discounts, among other benefits.

• Qualifications

• Physical Abilities
• While performing the duties of this job, the associate is often required to stand, walk, sit, use fine and gross motor skills, reach with hands and arms, balance, stoop, kneel, crouch, talk, hear, and smell.
• An individual in this position will be required to lift or carry weight in up to 50 lbs. Intermittent physical activity includes lifting and supporting residents. The associate must use proper body mechanics.

Weekend Warrior Program-Frequently Asked Questions

The following Q&A provides clarification regarding eligibility, scheduling, compensation, and expectations for participation in the Weekend Warrior Program:

1. Are Team Members (TMs) in the community eligible to enroll in the Weekend Warrior Program?

Yes. Team Members working in the community are eligible to transition into the Weekend Warrior Program if they wish to give up the weekday work schedule/commitment. This is a weekend only position.

2. What days are considered part of the Weekend Warrior schedule?

Weekend Warrior schedules are individualized based on the needs of each community. The designated schedule may include a combination of Thursday through Monday, depending on community staffing needs.

The program is not limited exclusively to Saturday and Sunday. For example, a Team Member who consistently works a Thursday–Monday schedule may qualify as a Weekend Warrior. This is based upon community needs. ED determines the need.

3. What are the rates for the Weekend Warrior Program for each role?

Weekend Warrior rates are individualized based on the community's established hourly rates for each role. The Weekend Warrior rate should be set at $1.00 more per hour than the applicable standard hourly rate.

4. If a Team Member currently works only weekends, are they considered a Weekend Warrior and eligible for the increased rate?

Team Members who consistently work the designated Weekend Warrior schedule may qualify for the program and associated rate increase. Communities should first identify Team Members who are regularly scheduled to work every weekend and determine whether their existing schedule meets the Weekend Warrior criteria.

5. What are the scheduling guidelines for the Weekend Warrior Program?

The Weekend Warrior Program is intended for Team Members who are hired and scheduled to work weekends, rather than Team Members who simply pick up additional weekend shifts or work EOW, as part of their regular schedule.  Working EOW along with their weekday schedule does not qualify for this program.  However, a Team Member who is hired to work Thursday through Monday every week could meet the intended scheduling structure for the program. Again, ED determines the community's need.

The program is therefore based on a consistent, recurring weekend-focused schedule, not by occasionally picking up one or more additional weekend shifts. Those that are hired to work weekends only, either every weekend or some commitment of routinely scheduled weekends.

jobs.title: Structural Engineer – Bridge & Transportation Structures
jobs.description:
AECOM’s Greater Pennsylvania Area Bridge (GPA) Engineering Practice is seeking an experienced Structural Engineer with a passion for bridge design. This is an excellent opportunity to work within a well-established and very successful bridge design group that offers a diverse range of projects, technical challenges, and career development opportunities.

Our GPA Bridge Engineering Practice works on projects for our local clients, as well as mega-projects throughout North America. These projects are delivered across many clients via various delivery methods. The GPA Bridge Engineering Practice has offices in Philadelphia, PA, Conshohocken, PA, Mechanicsburg, PA, Pittsburgh, PA, and Morgantown, WV. This Structural Engineer role is a hybrid role, working a minimum of 2 days from one of these AECOM offices and the remaining days remotely each week.

As populations grow, so do demands for safe, expedient and cost-effective transportation. Our Greater Pennsylvania Area Bridge Engineering Practice partners with our clients to build, modernize and expand transportation projects that carry all our communities into the future — safely and reliably. We use our extensive knowledge in planning, designing and managing transportation systems — as well as restoring and replacing aging infrastructure — to help our public and private clients find smarter, more advanced ways to move people across cities, countries and continents.

The responsibilities of the Structural Engineer position include, but are not limited to:

• Conceptual, preliminary and detailed final design of new bridges and other transportation structures;
• Analysis and rehabilitation design of existing bridges;
• Use of computer software for the analysis and design of bridges and other structures;
• Preparation and/or quality review checking of technical reports, design calculations, and structural plans;
• Preparation and/or quality review checking of technical specifications and construction cost estimates;
• Working both independently and with groups of engineers, designers and/or specialists toward the development of structural design documents and contract deliverables;
• Following of QA/QC procedures to ensure the technical quality of deliverables, and assisting with responses to client’s comments on structural design elements of the deliverables.
• Training, mentoring and helping to develop junior structural engineering staff; and
• Structural-related project task management.

Current Projects

Below are some of the major, local bridge and bridge corridor projects that our GPA Bridge Engineering Practice is currently working on:

• I-95/Girard Avenue Interchange Reconstruction, PennDOT District 6-0
• I-80 17M Total Reconstruction, PennDOT District 5-0
• I-81 D46 Total Reconstruction, PennDOT District 4-0
• I-95/US322 Interchange Reconstruction, PennDOT District 6-0
• I-70 K30 Mainline Reconstruction, PennDOT District 12-0
• McKeesport-Duquesne Bridge Rehabilitation, PennDOT District 11
• I-80 Brookville West, PennDOT District 10-0
• I-276 Widening and Reconstruction (Milepost 311 – Milepost 319), Pennsylvania Turnpike Commission
• Commodore Barry Bridge Structural Rehabilitation and Painting, Delaware River Port Authority
• Schuylkill to Suburban (S2S) Infrastructure Renewal Project, SEPTA
• SR 299 Viaduct over Appoquinimink River, DelDOT
• In addition, several of our Bridge Engineering Practice personnel are currently supporting mega design-build projects across North America

Minimum Requirements

• Bachelor's Degree in Civil Engineering with structures focus and four (4) years of relevant experience working on bridges and other transportation structures or demonstrated equivalency of experience and/or education
• Professional Engineering License (PE)
• Valid U.S. Driver’s License and as a condition of employment, must pass AECOM’s motor vehicle records review.

Preferred Qualifications

• Master’s Degree in Structural Engineering
• Six (6) or more years of experience with structural bridge design
• Project experience with PennDOT, Pennsylvania Turnpike Commission and/or other State DOTs
• Proficiency with CAD and similar computer software
• Experience in Finite Element Analysis using CSiBridge or other bridge FE analysis software
• Experience in BIM delivery and/or modeling using Bentley Open Bridge Modeler (OBM) or other modeling software
• Experience with alternative delivery methods or projects with early contractor involvement

• Sponsorship for US employment authorization is not available now or in the future for this position.
• Relocation assistance is not available for this position.
• This is a hybrid position. The selected candidate must be able to work on-site in Philadelphia, PA, Conshohocken, PA, Mechanicsburg, PA, Pittsburgh, PA, or Morgantown, WV a minimum of two days per week.

The Paraprofessional role is defined by the diverse learning needs of a student or group of students, as defined by their Individual Education Plan (IEP) or 504 plan, and in accordance with ISBE's student to teacher class size expectations. Paraprofessional positions are allocated and assigned annually based on student needs and may be subject to change. Expectations specific to the Paraprofessional role include but are not limited to:

Direct Student Support and IEP Documentation

• Actively engage students within daily instructional time to meet learning goals, during both whole-group, small group, and 1:1 instruction with materials and guidance from teachers
• Implement all interventions and behavior strategies as outlined in the student’s IEP or 504 plan
• Support with necessary student personal needs (hygiene, medical) and/or assisted technology and augmentative devices if noted in the IEP or 504 plan
• Support with assignment completion and reiteration of classroom instruction to improve academic outcomes
• Support with implementation of accommodations during class, district and state assessments
• Implement accommodations, scaffolds, and modifications to core curriculum as directed by the teacher to ensure access to grade-level content
• Provide behavioral management, effectively implementing de-escalation strategies as needed

• Maintain consistent weekly data tracking to monitor student growth, leveraging these insights during collaborative reflections with providers to drive data-informed adjustments to student interventions
• Maintain logs in SSM and contribute to Para Justification completion in readiness for the student’s IEP + 504 plan
• Actively participate in IEP + 504 meetings, providing meaningful input regarding the students performance

School-wide Culture & Instruction Responsibilities

• Collaborate with Gen Ed teachers, Diverse Learners teachers, and Case Managers to ensure the requirements of students’ IEPs are met and lessons are effectively reinforced
• Be responsive to direction and incorporate feedback from General Education Teacher, Diverse Learning Teacher, Case Manager and Principal
• Utilize school-wide systems and expectations for student culture effectively
• Adhere to individual schedule and support assigned students and classes as determined by Case Manager
• Model professional and ethical standards when interacting with students, staff, and parent/guardians
• Actively participate in school professional development and regional Paraprofessional professional development
• Participates in Safety Care training and other school-based and CPS trainings to ensure student safety
• Maintain prompt and consistent attendance to work and assigned responsibilities during daily school hours
• Maintain and model professional communication, work habits, and interpersonal interactions at all times

School-wide Duties

• Actively monitor daily arrival and dismissal post, aligned with school-wide schedule and expectations
• Actively monitor assigned late-pick up when assigned, aligned with school-wide schedule and expectations
• Support school day transitions and routines (lunch, restrooms, recess, etc.) within assigned student(s) schedule

REQUIREMENTS

• Active Paraprofessional (PARA) or Substitute (SUB) license with Illinois Board of Education (ISBE)
• Ability to work assigned schedule with prompt daily attendance, in accordance with regional time off policy Monday - Thursday: 7:30 AM - 4:05 PM Attend 1 after school meeting 4:00 - 4:45 PM on a day Mon. - Thurs established by school for professional learning community (Grade Level Team or Department)Friday: 7:30 AM - 4:00 PM (school-based professionals development after early dismissal) Total hours: 43.5 (40 + 3.5 overtime)
• Frequently standing or walking, using stairs to move throughout the school building; ability to lift / carry up to 10 lbs when necessary and/or support any required physical support needs in student IEP / 504 plan
• Cleared CPS background check & Faith’s Law attestation

Preferred experience and/or willingness to learn:

• Previous successful experience serving students with diverse learning needs to meet/exceed their IEP/504 goals
• Previous successful experience of accurate data collection for IEP goals and documentation
• Previous successful experience utilizing effective SEL and behavioral management strategies with students
• Previous successful experience utilizing Google Suite (Gmail, Sheets, Docs)

COMPENSATION

• Competitive rates for medical insurance and short-term disability insurance. Dental insurance, vision insurance, life insurance, and long-term disability insurance are offered at no cost.

jobs.description:
ABOUT SUNO

We're building the world's first creative entertainment platform, where the entire world can feel the joy and fulfillment of making music. Music is for everyone: Our users include everyone from grandmothers creating songs for their loved ones, to Grammy winners using Suno Studio, our power tool, to make the most popular hits in the world.

Building the future of entertainment requires ambition. The pace is fast, the problems are hard, and the work demands ownership and intensity. For the right people, it’s incredibly rewarding: a chance to shape a new medium, work with a small team that cares deeply about quality, make music, drink too much coffee, and build something that millions of people use to express themselves in ways that were never before possible.

Suno is the fastest growing consumer entertainment company and the leader in AI music. We are backed by leading investors including Bond Capital, Menlo Ventures, Lightspeed Venture Partners, IVP, Forerunner, Union Square Ventures, Alkeon, Quiet, Matrix Partners, Schroders Capital and, NVentures (venture arm of NVIDIA).




ABOUT THE ROLE

Suno is changing who gets to make music, and this role helps bring that to millions of new people. As Creative Strategy Lead, you'll own the creative strategy behind our performance marketing: which audiences we reach, what resonates with each, and how every ad makes us smarter. You'll lead a team of creative specialists, work hand-in-hand with paid media, data science, and production, and build the playbook for how we grow, with full autonomy to shape it.

Listen to the song we made about it: https://suno.com/s/wSfvXxWs5tF0RkeL




WHAT YOU’LL DO

 - Build a persona playbook that spells out what to say, show, and test for each audience, and keep it current as results come in

 - Run the loop from creative analysis to insight to strategy, partnering with paid media and data science on tagging, testing, and reading what drove performance

 - Drive audience research, customer conversations, and competitive intel to deepen our understanding of who we bring in, scale what works, and find new audiences worth reaching

 - Lead and develop a team of creative specialists across UGC, AI, and brand creative, and manage our UGC agency partner

 - Feed what you learn about our users back into product and go-to-market, and help bring millions of new people into creative entertainment




WHAT YOU’LL NEED

 - 8+ years in creative strategy, with deep roots in performance marketing

 - A track record of paid social creative strategy that drove subscriptions and conversions (not brand or awareness campaigns), with results you can speak to

 - Experience at large, complex consumer companies with a wide range of audiences, selling everything from low-price subscriptions to higher-ticket plans

 - Experience leading creative strategists and creatives while acting as the bridge between creative and paid media teams

 - A sharp, clear communicator who can explain exactly how a strategy is built and why

 - Relentlessly proactive: you go looking for the audience insight nobody handed you, and you care deeply about the people you're advertising to

 - Bonus: YouTube or Google display creative, ASO, or lifecycle marketing experience

Additional Notes:

 - Applicants must be eligible to work in the US.

 - This role requires working onsite at one of our offices.

 


PERKS & BENEFITS FOR FULL-TIME EMPLOYEES

jobs.title: Managing Director of School Operations, High Schools
jobs.description:
The Managing Director of School Operations for High Schools (HS MDSO) owns operational excellence at our two Newark high schools. Our high schools, including their operations, are not yet where our students need them to be. This role exists to change that. The HS MDSO sets an uncompromising bar for what excellent high school operations look like, models it personally, and demands it from every Director of Campus Operations (DCO) and ops team they lead.

The role starts with improving and supporting the schools we have: attendance, enrollment and 8th-to-9th persistence, safe and beautiful buildings, and systems that protect every instructional minute. It grows into building the operational standard that defines a KIPP Newark high school.

The HS MDSO reports to the Managing Director of Operations (MDO) and works in close partnership with the Managing Director of High Schools, who leads academic outcomes for the same schools. Academics and operations work toward one shared set of goals for the same students.

Scope of Responsibility

• Newark high schools: Direct management of the DCOs at our two Newark high schools; be accountable, jointly with each School Leader, for their success and the performance of their ops teams.
• High school leadership: Operations partner to the Managing Director of High Schools and the high school School Leaders.
• Regional and network: Works with Newark regional and network operations teams to set, standardize, and improve high school operational systems.

Priorities

Priority 1: Raise the bar on high school operations now

This is the first job and the one that matters most in year one. Every system in both buildings should be joyful, safe, and efficient, and should protect instructional time.

• Name the non-negotiables for high school operations, set clear expectations and owners for every system and project, and hold the line.
• Inspect what we expect. Walk systems (such as arrival, dismissal, meals, attendance, and transitions) with each DCO before the year begins and throughout it, confirming that execution matches design, and coach in real time.
• Run monthly audits of materials and systems and quarterly reviews to find what broke down, what can be streamlined, and where instructional minutes are being lost.
• Set and hold the expectation of a beautiful school: clean, orderly, bright spaces that tell students and staff they are valued here.
• Close every loop. Follow problems through to real resolution, name whether they are school, regional, or network problems, and bring in the right people.

Priority 2: Coach and develop DCOs to an excellent bar

Our DCOs and ops teams get better because this person coaches them directly, gives frank feedback, and models what excellent looks like.

• Hold weekly one-on-ones with each DCO and weekly/bi-weekly observations of each school's operational systems, processes, and meetings.
• Coach the coach: observe how DCOs lead their teams, give feedback on the questions they ask, and push them to see around corners.
• Address underperformance directly and constructively, as soon as it appears.
• Review DCO project plans (state testing, events, safety) against a clear bar before execution, and lead debriefs and after-action reviews that lead to fast iteration.
• Lead tabletop exercises on emergencies and high-stakes days so every ops leader has answered "what happens if ___" before it happens.
• Design professional development pathways for every school ops role so that high-performing ops teams exist in both schools, and step in to serve in a school operations capacity when coverage is needed.

Priority 3: Drive the operational outcomes that matter for high school students

Ops success is measured by student and family outcomes, not task completion or effort.

• Attendance: Own a high school attendance plan with regional partners. Give feedback on, hold a high bar for, and internalize each school's plan; hold DCOs accountable to it and coach pivots when it isn't working. Sit side by side with DCOs to remove barriers when a school is off track.
• Data: Lead weekly DKI spaces so DCOs internalize the data, share topline goals and progress to goal, and leave with a plan. Progress monitor every action item to completion.
• Enrollment and persistence: Coach DCOs to 100% completion on all enrollment metrics. Analyze persistence trends across both schools, bring a K-12 pipeline perspective, and hold DCOs accountable to executing 8th-to-9th transition plans.
• Safety: Make sure drill tracking is in place and drills happen on cadence, safety plans are current, and every adult knows their role before an emergency.
• Families: Ensure every family interaction and onboarding experience is warm, clear, and easy to navigate, especially for families with the least bandwidth.
• Academic Operations: Ensure highest possible academic outcomes for our students through maximized academic operations aligned to our priorities, including workstreams such as testing, transcripts, report cards, and office hours.

Priority 4: Steward resources toward student needs

• Internalize and communicate how the organization and region prioritizes resource allocation, and keep a regional perspective at all times.
• Review each school's monthly budget analysis and raise flags when a DCO does not see the consequences of their budget choices.
• Confirm that schools have the non-negotiable materials and resources, and the budget, to execute their vision.

Priority 5: Build one high school standard and align partners around it

• Standardize the processes that should be consistent across both high schools, document them, and build playbooks so any teammate can execute them.
• Observe across schools to find common gaps and misalignment (student sign-out, visitor management, state testing, and more), and close them.
• Partner with the Managing Director of High Schools and School Leaders so academic and operational priorities stay aligned.
• Collaborate with high school partners across Student Experience, KIPP Forward, Teaching & Learning, Special Education, Athletics, and academic operations.
• Lead initiatives aligned to regional priorities such as 8th-to-9th persistence, safety and security, and resource allocation.
• Work with regional and network departments on technology, facilities, nutrition, compliance, and enrollment, and support the COO and MDO in identifying network-wide system improvements.

Key Outcomes

School operations performance

• Student attendance and chronic absenteeism
• Enrollment targets met and maintained, and 8th-to-9th persistence
• Operations walkthrough and audit results against the regional standard
• Safety drill and compliance completion
• Healthy fiscal management (0–3% of budget remaining at year-end)

Talent development

• Growth and retention of strong DCOs and school operations teammates
• A bench of ops leaders ready for the next role

Must Have:

• Experience and results in a school-based operations leadership role
• Direct management experience, with a record of developing leaders and holding a high bar
• 5–10 years of work experience, preferably in business or operations management
• K-12 education experience preferred
• Bachelor's degree required; Master's degree preferred

You will thrive in this role if you:

• Hold an extremely high bar, models it personally, and is comfortable demanding it from others
• Give direct, specific feedback and seeks it for their own leadership
• Own your outcomes and wants to be held accountable for them
• Work with urgency, closes loops, and names risks before they become crises
• Build trusting relationships and works across teams to get results for kids
• Stay calm and steady on high-stakes days and brings that energy to the people around them
• Have a passion for the mission, vision, and values of KIPP Team & Family

Compensation & Benefits

KIPP Team & Family offers a market-competitive salary ranging from $162,000–$182,000 based on experience. Salary ranges are set by role level and function using benchmarks in the education and nonprofit sector and allow for growth within the role. Individual compensation is set based on factors including relevant professional experience and qualifications; education, skills, and training; and market conditions.

In addition to a competitive salary, we a generous benefits package including, but not limited to, the following:

• Robust benefits that include medical, dental, and vision
• Optional participation in the KIPP NJ 403b retirement plan, including matching contributions
• A school-issued laptop
• Transportation benefits for TEAMmates commuting into Newark from the New York City area
• Generous time off including some school vacation weeks (depending on the year), allocated sick and personal days, and an extended summer break
• Up to 12 weeks 100% parental leave for primary caregivers
• Employer paid life insurance
• Extensive optional ancillary benefits including, short term and long term disability and accident and hospital indemnity

jobs.title: Senior Data Engineer
jobs.description:
ABOUT E2B

E2B is a fast-growing Series A startup with over $37M in funding and 8-figure revenue. We are building the Agent Cloud and power the infrastructure behind AI labs and some of the most widely used consumer and enterprise agents, including Manus, Genspark, Lindy, Groq, and Artificial Analysis. Our team includes original authors of Firecracker, the AWS microVM technology powering Lambda, along with alumni of Cognition, JetBrains, Zapier, and Wish.




ABOUT THE ROLE

We’re looking for a Senior Data Engineer to build the data foundation that helps us understand our business and make better decisions.

You’ll turn data across our infrastructure, billing, and business systems into reliable pipelines and clearly defined datasets. You’ll join the engineering team, report to our Head of Engineering, and work closely with our Head of Finance as your primary partner initially. Over time, your work will support Growth, GTM, and other teams across E2B.

We have data and pieces of the foundation in place. You’ll help bring them together, establish the missing building blocks, and own the quality and usefulness of what we deliver.

You’ll have direct access to the people using your work and substantial ownership over how E2B’s data foundation develops. Your work will help teams answer important questions independently, spend less time reconciling numbers, and make decisions with confidence.

Responsibilities include:

 - Build and operate pipelines that bring operational and business data into our warehouse, including sandbox usage, cloud infrastructure, billing, and accounting data.

 - Create data models and shared metric definitions that teams can understand and use consistently.

 - Establish testing, monitoring, reconciliation, and alerting to catch missing data, inconsistencies, and unexpected changes.

 - Partner with Finance to turn business questions into dependable datasets, starting with usage, revenue, costs, and margins.

 - Make data accessible for self-service analysis, reporting, and AI-assisted querying through clear structure and documentation.

 - Work with engineering teams to improve source data quality and resolve issues from ingestion through downstream consumption.

 - Make practical decisions about architecture and tooling, balancing immediate business needs with maintainability.


WHAT WE’RE LOOKING FOR

 - Experience building and owning production data pipelines and warehouse models, including establishing foundations where systems were incomplete or fragmented.

 - Strong SQL and Python skills, with sound software engineering practices around testing, version control, deployment, and monitoring.

 - Experience with a cloud data warehouse such as BigQuery, Snowflake, or Redshift, and tools for data transformation and orchestration.

 - A track record of working directly with business stakeholders, clarifying ambiguous requirements, and connecting technical work to business outcomes.

 - The ability to investigate discrepancies, understand their root causes, and make the underlying systems more reliable.

 - Strong ownership: you can identify what needs to happen, prioritize it, and carry it through without detailed instructions.

We expect this experience will often come from around six or more years of relevant work, but the depth of your ownership and what you’ve built matter more than a specific number.




BONUS POINTS FOR:

 - Building data foundations at a startup or on a small team.

 - Supporting Finance, Revenue Operations, Growth, or GTM.

 - Working with usage-based products, billing data, or cloud infrastructure costs.

 - Building well-documented datasets that support self-service analytics and AI tools.

Finance domain expertise is helpful, but it isn’t required. We’re looking for an engineer who is curious about the business, learns quickly, and takes responsibility for delivering data people can trust.




WHAT IT’S LIKE TO WORK AT E2B

We’re a fast-growing startup with in-person (4 days on-site, 1 day WFH) offices in San Francisco and Prague, Czech Republic. We already generate 8-figure revenue and work directly with top-tier AI companies like Manus, Genspark, Lindy, Groq, Artificial Analysis and other exciting teams pushing the frontier of AI.

We offer healthcare, vision, and dental insurance, unlimited PTO, 401k, and a variety of perks for in-office employees.

jobs.description:

At Cresco Labs, we aim to revolutionize and lead the nation’s cannabis industry with a focus on quality and consistency of product, and to bring legitimacy to the industry with the highest level of integrity and professionalism.

If you’re interested in joining our mission, click the below links to join our team today!

MISSION STATEMENT

At Cresco, we aim to lead the nation’s cannabis industry with a focus on regulatory compliance, product consistency, and customer satisfaction. Our operations bring legitimacy to the cannabis industry by acting with the highest level of integrity, strictly adhering to regulations, and promoting the clinical efficacy of cannabis. As Cresco grows, we will operate with the same level of professionalism and precision in each new market we move in to.

JOB SUMMARY

The Wellness Advisor of Sunnyside* will be responsible for advising customers (recreational, medicinal and caregivers) in selecting the proper cannabis products for their needs and act as an ambassador of the company’s mission to normalize, professionalize and revolutionize cannabis. You will use your customer service, product knowledge and adherence to state compliance regulations to ensure a best-in-class experience. Wellness Advisors are responsible for the customer lifecycle from check-in to consultation, order fulfillment to checkout. In this role, compliance with applicable state and company regulations will be at the forefront of all tasks.

At Sunnyside, we believe the employee experience is paramount to all. With a strong focus on training, development, diversity and authenticity, our employees experience both personal and professional growth.  As a Wellness Advisor, you will have:

• The opportunity to learn fundamental cannabis product knowledge & industry compliance standards.

• The training to navigate different customer interactions and circumstances.

• A unique sales experience leading with a consultative & personalized approach.

• Experience in a dynamic role that combines problem solving, inventory management, teamwork, technical skills, and customer service!

Our dispensaries are typically open 7 days a week, and we value flexibility to work across opening and closing shifts, as well as weekends and holidays. Part-time schedules will be 15-25 hours a week, and typically based around peak hours.

WHO YOU ARE

• You are energetic, possess strong interpersonal skills and work well with others. Collaboration is key to our team’s success!

• You enjoy people! Consulting our customers, listening to their needs and providing an exceptional experience is vital to achieving customer loyalty.

• You are resilient and agile! You use challenges as opportunities to acquire or master skills!

CORE JOB DUTIES

In accordance with any local and state compensation laws, the compensation listed is the current estimated range for the position. $16—$16 USD

BENEFITS

Cresco Labs is proud to offer eligible employees a robust offering of benefits including, major medical, dental and vision insurance, a 401(K)-match program, FSA/HSA programs, LTD/STD options, life insurance and AD&D.  We also offer eligible employees paid holidays and paid time off.  Other rewards may include annual discretionary bonuses, stock options as well as participation in our employee discount program. Benefits eligibility for permanent positions may vary by full-time or part-time roles, location, or position.

ADDITIONAL REQUIREMENTS

• Must be 21 years of age or older to apply

• Must comply with all legal or company regulations for working in the industry

• The company does not offer employment-based visa sponsorship for this role or any other position, now or in the future. Applicants must be legally authorized to work in the United States on a permanent basis without the need for current or future sponsorship at any time.

Cresco Labs is an Equal Opportunity Employer and all applicants will be considered without attention to race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, national origin, veteran, or disability status.

California Consumer Privacy Act (“CCPA”) Notice to Applicants: Please read the California Employee Privacy Notice (“CA Privacy Notice”) regarding Sunnyside* and its affiliate Cresco Labs’ policies pertaining to the collection, use, and disclosure of personal information. This CA Privacy Notice supplements the information contained in the Sunnyside* Privacy Policy and applies to California resident employees and job applicants. Applicants with disabilities may access this notice in an alternative format by contacting CCPAnotice@crescolabs.com Reporting a Scam:

jobs.title: Senior Quality Operations Specialist, CAP & Monitoring
jobs.description:
At WelbeHealth, we serve our communities’ most vulnerable seniors through shared intention, pioneering spirit, and the courage to love. These core values and our participant focus lead the way no matter what.

Under the direct supervision of the Quality Operations Director, the Senior Quality Operations Specialist, CAP & Monitoring leads the development, implementation, and monitoring of corrective action plans (CAPs) related to PACE regulatory audit findings. This role partners with Operational, Clinical, Compliance, and Quality leaders to drive accountability, resolve barriers, support timely closure, and validate sustained compliance. The Senior Quality Operations Specialist, CAP & Monitoring manages multiple CAPs, analyzes monitoring results, escalates risks, and supports continuous improvement.

This role is different because the Senior Quality Operations Specialist, CAP & Monitoring at WelbeHealth:

• Owns the end-to-end lifecycle of CAPs resulting from PACE regulatory audits, monitoring activities, complaints, and other compliance reviews from root cause analysis (RCA) and remediation planning through implementation, monitoring, validation, and sustained closure

• Serves as a cross-functional driver of regulatory remediation, partnering with leaders to identify risks, remove barriers, strengthen accountability, and use data and monitoring results to validate that corrective actions are effective and sustainable

We care about our team members. That’s why we offer:

• Medical insurance coverage (Medical, Dental, Vision)

• Work/life balance - We mean it! 17 days of personal time off (PTO), 12 holidays observed annually, and 6 sick days

• 401K savings + match

• Comprehensive compensation package including base pay and bonus

• And additional benefits!

On the day-to-day, you will:

• Lead the development, implementation, monitoring, and validation of CAPs resulting from PACE regulatory audits, mock audits, monitoring activities, complaints, and other compliance-related reviews, as well as proactively identify and escalate risks, overdue actions, implementation challenges, and systemic issues

• Partner with center and departmental leadership to develop remediation strategies, establish timelines, resolve barriers, and drive timely completion of corrective actions

• Facilitate CAP meetings, RCA, and remediation workgroups to support accountability and progress toward closure

• Review documentation, monitoring results, and evidence submissions to assess implementation effectiveness, sustainability, and compliance with regulatory requirements

• Develop and maintain CAP dashboards, tracking tools, reports, and status updates, as well as leverage data, monitoring results, and performance metrics to identify trends, risks, and opportunities for continuous improvement

• Identify opportunities to leverage AI and technology to automate workflows and improve operational effectiveness

• Support PACE regulatory audits, mock audits, complaint investigations, and other Quality Operations initiatives as assigned

Job requirements include:

• Bachelor’s degree in healthcare administration, nursing, public health, business administration, health information management, regulatory affairs, quality management, compliance, or related field required; master’s degree preferred

• Previous experience with process improvement, risk assessment, and quality improvement methodologies (e.g., PDSA, Lean, Six Sigma) preferred

• Minimum of three (3) years of experience in healthcare quality, compliance, auditing, performance improvement, corrective action management, or related operations; five (5) years of experience preferred

• Experience developing, implementing, monitoring, and sustaining regulatory CAPs

• Experience in RCA, PACE, Medicare, Medicaid, managed care, healthcare operations, quality, or compliance preferred

• Experience developing dashboards, reports, tracking tools, and performance measures; Power BI experience preferred

• Strong data-driven approach and critical-thinking skills, including identifying trends, evaluating risks, determining root causes, and developing actionable recommendations

• Ability to use AI and technology to automate workflows, streamline processes, and improve operational efficiency and effectiveness

• Travel to WelbeHealth centers as needed to support business-related activities, including occasional overnight stays

We are seeking a highly organized, analytical, and collaborative Senior Quality Operations Specialist, CAP & Monitoring who is passionate about quality, regulatory compliance, and driving meaningful operational improvement. The ideal candidate brings strong project management, critical-thinking, communication, and problem-solving skills, with the ability to manage multiple CAPs, engage cross-functional stakeholders, identify risks and root causes, and drive timely and sustainable resolution. If you thrive in a fast-paced environment, are comfortable navigating complexity and ambiguity, and are energized by using data, technology, and continuous improvement to strengthen compliance and operational performance, we’d love to hear from you.

Compensation consists of base salary plus bonus. WelbeHealth offers a competitive total rewards package that includes a 401(k) match, comprehensive healthcare coverage, and a broad range of additional benefits. Actual compensation will be determined based on experience and relevant qualifications.

Compensation Offering

$74,612.76—$98,488.84 USD

At WelbeHealth, our mission is to unlock the full potential of our vulnerable seniors. In this spirit, please note that we have a vaccination policy for all our employees and proof of vaccination, or a vaccine declination form will be required prior to employment. WelbeHealth maintains required infection control and PPE standards and has requirements relevant to all team members regarding vaccinations.

Our Commitment to Diversity, Equity and Inclusion

At WelbeHealth, we embrace and cherish the diversity of our team members, and we're committed to building a culture of inclusion and belonging. We're proud to be an equal opportunity employer. People seeking employment at WelbeHealth are considered without regard to race, color, religion, sex, gender, gender identity, gender expression, sexual orientation, marital or veteran status, age, national origin, ancestry, citizenship, physical or mental disability, medical condition, genetic information or characteristics (or those of a family member), pregnancy or other status protected by applicable law.

ABOUT US

Office Hours is an on-demand expert network that connects leading organizations with trusted experts across various knowledge domains. Experts earn income by sharing their knowledge through advisory work, projects, and AI model training. Our platform handles the complexities behind the scenes— screening, compliance, scheduling, and payments—so knowledge sharing stays focused on meaningful insights and real impact.

We’re a hyper-growth and profitable company, quickly expanding our expert network, launching new offices, and new products. WHAT WE BELIEVE

Our vision is to make human knowledge easily accessible and infinitely scalable by building tools for the new age knowledge economy.




ABOUT THE ROLE

As a Client Solutions Manager, you will own a portfolio of enterprise customers and will be directly responsible for their growth. jobs.title: Product Manager- Logistics
jobs.description:
ABOUT TENSEC

Tensec is Vertical AI for cross-border trade. Trade is two flows, money and goods, and the trading companies that move them: freight forwarders, shipping lines, customs brokers, 4PLs  — still run both on systems built for large corporations and a lot of manual work. Tensec is the agentic AI layer those companies use to move both flows for their importer and exporter clients: FX and payments today, quoting and booking next, trade finance to follow. Cross-border B2B is a $50 trillion market. We're building the version all global trading companies choose to use.

We started in the US, Mexico, and Brazil and are expanding globally, onboarding enterprise trading companies whose trade flows run to billions of dollars a year across every major corridor. Founded in 2023 by a team that has built and exited startups and run global teams at Meta, PayPal, Credit Karma, Goldman Sachs, Visa, Mastercard, and American Express. Tensec is backed by world-class investors such as Quiet Capital, Coinbase Ventures, Costanoa Ventures, Renegade Partners, Clocktower, and WillowTree.




YOUR MISSION

Getting freight across a border still runs on email and on the memory of whoever is handling it. Someone prices the request by hand against contracts and this month's surcharges, keys much of it in again to make the booking, then watches for what changes while the shipment moves. Most of what makes any of it go well lives in that person's experience rather than in a system. You are joining us to change this.

You will own the AI for that run of work: the request, the quote, the booking, and keeping the shipment honest while it moves. Those stages are your first year. They are also what everything downstream stands on, because the commercial and financial side of a forwarder only works as well as the shipment file underneath it.

This role has a forward deployment component, and we mean it literally. You will sit with our clients' pricing and operations teams, learn how the work actually happens, and design workflows that fit their process. Engineers build the connections into their systems, while you . You decide what moves between them, which parts of the work an agent takes, and where a person stays in the loop.

We are early in this product line. The first clients are how we find out what can be generalized and productized, and you will be the person making that call. If that is the interesting part of the job to you, this is your role.




OUTCOMES — YOUR FIRST 12–18 MONTHS

 - Get an agent into daily use inside a client's team within your first two quarters. One workflow, doing work a person did by hand the week before.

 - Establish the baseline nobody has today. Pick the few numbers that matter, measure them honestly before you build anything, and prove the improvement against them rather than asserting it.

 - Stop the handoffs losing information. What one stage decides should reach the next without being retyped, and what changes mid-shipment should reach the people it affects without someone remembering to forward an email.

 - Get the judgment out of people's heads and into the product. The calls experienced operators make without thinking are the product, and they need to survive the person who knows them leaving.

 - Set the accuracy bar for an AI system where a wrong number costs real money. Define what good means, build the eval set, design the confirmation step, and decide what an agent is never permitted to send unsupervised.

 - Turn client-specific work into product. For every workflow, make the call: bespoke, configurable, or core, and be able to defend it.

 - Bring the second and third clients onto the same product with materially less custom work than the first.
   
   


ALSO ON YOUR PLATE

 - Requirements gathering as a craft. Running sessions with pricing, operations and finance teams, and leaving with a process map they correct rather than politely accept.

 - Writing the specs and flows engineers build from, and staying close enough to the build to answer questions in hours rather than sprints.

 - Putting a working prototype in front of a client instead of a slide. You will build those yourself with AI tools.

 - Being the person the client's pricing lead calls. You own that relationship rather than handing it to an account manager.

 - Working through the hard cases rather than around them. The requests that do not fit the standard path, and everything that changes after a shipment is confirmed, are the workflow rather than the edge case.

 - Partnering with the freight expertise we already have in house, and helping shape what we charge for and how.
   
   


WHAT YOU BRING

 - 5+ years building or delivering software for operational teams, including at least one 0 to 1 you took from nothing to real usage. Product management is the most common path into this role, but we will read implementation leads, solutions leads and operators who moved into product with equal interest. We care more about trajectory than title.

 - Experience in a domain where the pricing and operational data is genuinely messy. You ask about the data model before you ask about the screen, and you know what a business rule looks like after ten years of being patched by hand.

 - You can read a process and see the data underneath it. Given two systems and a handoff between them, you can work out what each one owns, where the truth lives, what goes stale, and what breaks when a person is the integration.

 - Judgment about where AI belongs and where it does not. You can look at an operational workflow and say which parts an agent should own, which parts need a person, and which parts should stay deterministic because control matters more than cleverness.

 - Hands-on with AI, in the way a product person is. You have built with LLMs yourself, even if only in prototypes, you are comfortable with prompting, retrieval and evaluation, and you can tell a demo that works from a system that works. You do not need to write production code.

 - You are good in a room with a customer. You can run a working session with people who have been burned by software before, and leave with them on your side.

 - You can hold your own with engineers without doing their job. You ask good questions about what a system can and cannot give you, and you know when "that's hard" means hard and when it means tedious.

 - Working Spanish is a plus. Our client pricing teams work in Spanish, and the signal you need is often in what they say to each other rather than in what gets translated for you. Not a gate if everything else is there.

 - Based in Miami, NYC, or Palo Alto, and willing to travel on site with clients in the US and Latin America.
   
   


HOW YOU WORK

 - You go and look. A day shadowing a pricer beats a well-run interview, and you would rather do both.

 - High agency, high urgency. You decide and move rather than waiting for a room to converge.

 - You say no to some of the wish list items. Clients will give you twenty ideas. You ship the one that moves the number, and you can explain that choice to their CEO.

 - You write. Specs, decisions, and what you learned this week, so the rest of the company can build on it.

 - You hold a date. When something is going to slip you say so early and propose a smaller version rather than a later one.

 - You would rather ship a narrow thing that works than a broad thing that demos.
   
   


NICE TO HAVE

 - Freight forwarding, customs brokerage, 3PL or logistics technology background. A real plus, and not a requirement. We have deep freight expertise in house and you will be working alongside it daily.

 - You have built quoting, rating, tariff or pricing systems in any industry.

 - Experience with transport management, rate management or procurement platforms, or with the carrier and marketplace rate sources behind them.

 - You have shipped a product with a significant LLM component.

 - Consulting or solutions delivery experience, particularly if you have since moved to the product side and know where the two disagree.

 - Experience in Brazil or Mexico, or building for Latin American SMBs.

Even if you don't meet 100% of the qualifications, we encourage you to apply.




COMPENSATION & BENEFITS

The expected salary range for this role is $180,000 to $225,000 per year in New York or Palo Alto, and $160,000 to $190,000 per year in Miami. Actual compensation will depend on experience, skills, and qualifications.

 - Equity

 - Medical, dental and vision

 - 15 days paid time off

 - Learning and development budget
   
   


EQUAL OPPORTUNITY

Tensec is an Equal Opportunity Employer. We do not discriminate on the basis of race, color, religion, sex, national origin, age, disability, veteran status, sexual orientation, gender identity, or any other characteristic protected by federal, state, or local law.

Tensec is a diverse and inclusive company committed to growing a diverse and inclusive team. We invite people of all backgrounds and identities to apply. Additionally, we encourage everyone to share which pronouns you wish for us to use when addressing you (i.e., she/her, he/him, they/them).

We are committed to providing reasonable accommodations for qualified individuals with disabilities. Please let your recruiter know if you require an accommodation during the application or interview process.

Even if you don't meet 100% of the qualifications, we encourage you to apply.

jobs.title: Emergency Credentialed Veterinary Technician - Willow Grove, PA
jobs.description:
ABOUT VEG

In 2014, VEG was born with a mission to help people and their pets when they need it most. This meant challenging the status quo and fixing everything that was wrong with the ER experience. Since then, we’ve expanded rapidly, with hospitals nationwide open 24/7, 365 days a year, and created a better emergency experience—not only for people and their pets, but also for everyone who works here—our VEGgies!

At VEG we find a way to say yes to the career you want in veterinary emergency medicine. This means transforming how ER works, from our open-concept hospitals, where you can handle emergency cases of every kind (even exotics!) to our immersive, customer-focused experience, which helps us give people and their pets the care they deserve.

This also means saying yes to creating the greatest experience possible for our VEGgies. Yes to working in an environment where you can find your place and feel valued for the amazing work you do. Yes to having unparalleled opportunities for learning and mentorship so you can grow where you want to go in your career. And yes to making an impact here in ways you never thought possible.

VEG is a 2025 and 2026 certified Great Place to Work®.

THE JOB

As an Emergency Credentialed Veterinary Technician, you’re part of a team that thrives on the front lines of emergency veterinary care where every second counts. You’ll handle a wide range of cases, from minor to complex emergencies, collaborating with our doctors and team in delivering gold standard, emotionally intelligent care. You’ll jump into triage, treatments, diagnostics, anesthesia, monitoring, and critical care nursing, all while being a steady, compassionate presence for pet parents in their most stressful moments. This role is for someone who wants to do the work they were trained to do (and more), continue growing their skills, and help people and their pets when they need it most.

WHAT YOU’LL DO

• Treat every patient and person like they matter—because they do! You keep people and pets together and stay by their side through tests, treatments, and everything in between

• Jump into action, delivering nursing care, treatments, and emotional support in the most critical moments, from triage to discharge

• Bring the meds, the monitoring, and the mastery—from IVs and CRIs to blood transfusions and beyond

• Communicate like a teammate and think like a leader, helping shape plans and keep care flowing

• Be ready to perform CPR like the trained RECOVER rockstar you are (not only do we offer training, we have the highest number of RECOVER CPR professionals and instructors in the industry!)

• All the techy stuff—from diagnostics and imaging to sample collection and placing tubes

• Anesthesia, even for our most fragile patients? You’ve got it.

• Use all the advanced techniques in your toolkit: central lines, endoscopy, ultrasounds, and more

WHAT YOU NEED

• High school diploma or equivalent required; associate’s degree or higher in veterinary technology from an AVMA accredited program strongly preferred

• Credentialed as a Veterinary Technician (CVT, RVT, LVT, LVMT) in the state the VEG practice is located is required; VTS in ECC, internal medicine or anesthesia/analgesia is a plus and will lead to extra considerations in compensation

• 1+ years of experience in a veterinary technician role; experience in emergency or specialty medicine preferred

• Basic computer skills and a comprehension of practice management software and electronic medical record keeping

• Excellent communicator and calm under pressure; ready to lend a hand to support those around you

• Fine motor skills for handling patients and medical equipment

• Ability to stand for prolonged hours, kneel, and work on the floor as well as ability to lift up to 25 kg on own and able to support up to 40 kg with assistance

• Must be willing to work in a noisy environment with strong or unpleasant odors.

• Availability to work nights, weekends, and holidays on a rotating or as needed basis based on hospital needs

• Work well in a fast-paced environment with people from all backgrounds and different personality types

WHO YOU ARE

• Empathetic, instinctively taking a people-centric approach, whether supporting your colleagues or making an effort to understand different perspectives

• Have a sense of humility; acknowledging mistakes, sharing credit with others, and lifting up your team’s’ accomplishments

• Feel a strong sense of ownership over your work, taking responsibility for outcomes and staying committed to achieving long-term, impactful results

• Curious by nature; you ask insightful questions and continuously seek out opportunities to learn and grow your skills and knowledge

IonQ’s newest generation of quantum computers, the IonQ Tempo, is the latest in a line of cutting-edge systems that have been helping customers and partners including Amazon Web Services, and AstraZeneca achieve 20x performance results and accelerate innovation in drug discovery, materials science, financial modeling, logistics, cybersecurity, and defense. Our quantum computing services are available through all major cloud providers, while we also meet the needs of networking and sensing customers across land, sea, air, and space. IonQ is making quantum platforms more accessible and impactful than ever before.

Location: This role is based onsite at our office in Chattanooga, TN and can work remotely up to 3 days per week.
Travel: Normally about 25% to customer sites, including international travel; longer continuous on-site periods during commissioning
Job ID:  1936

The Role:

IonQ builds quantum network data centers as a distinct product line, providing infrastructure that enables researchers and customers to run distributed quantum experiments. We're looking for a Quantum Network Support Engineer to join our team supporting these networks once they're built and handed off.

This role can be hands-on. You'll work with fiber optics, photon detectors, interferometers, and other quantum network hardware in both lab and datacenter environments. You'll also work directly with customers, helping translate their experimental needs into working network topologies. Candidates with backgrounds in photonics, fiber optics, optical engineering, or physics are encouraged to apply. The role normally involves about 25% travel to customer sites, including international travel. Commissioning phases may require longer continuous periods on site

Responsibilities:

• Maintain quantum network hardware, including fiber interconnects, passive optical components, and control electronics in datacenter rack environments.
• Assist in commissioning new quantum network deployments at customer sites, including extended on-site assignments as networks come online.
• Characterize network performance after changes using instruments such as OTDRs, power meters, polarimeters, and photon detectors.
• Respond to support tickets to troubleshoot network faults: trace logical and physical signal paths, isolate root causes, resolve issues or implement workarounds, and communicate changes to affected customers.
• Consult with researchers and customers on network topology design: translating experimental requirements into loss-budgeted fiber path plans that account for distance, polarization, and timing constraints.
• Document network configurations, characterization data, and procedures in a clear and accessible way.

Requirements:

• Bachelor's degree in physics, optics, electrical engineering, or a related science.
• Hands-on comfort with fiber optic handling: connectors, cleaning, and slack management.
• Familiarity with basic networking concepts: IP addressing, subnets, interfaces, LAN/WAN.
• Strong written and verbal communication. You'll support users ranging from graduate students to principal investigators across technical and non-technical contexts.
• A systematic troubleshooting mindset. Able to isolate a problem methodically and comfortable saying "I don't know, let me find out."
• Desire to learn and improve through training and self-study.
• Willingness to work flexible hours and travel to customer sites, including extended periods on site during commissioning.

Preferred Qualifications:
• Experience with optical test equipment: OTDR, optical power meters, fiber scopes, and visual fault locators.
• Hands-on lab experience in quantum or classical optics.
• Working knowledge of quantum networking concepts.
• Experience with Python or other scripting languages.
• A background in data analysis or data science.
• Background in atomic or optical physics. Experience with laser stabilization, AOMs, or vacuum systems is a strong plus.

The total compensation package includes base, bonus, equity, and a range of benefit options found on our career site.

If this role has a commission structure, the compensation range below just reflects the base compensation range.

$124,000—$155,000 USD

Compensation will vary based on individual factors such as education, qualifications, and experience of the final candidate(s), specific office location, and calibration against relevant market data and internal team equity. Posted base salary figures are subject to change as new market data becomes available. Our benefits include comprehensive medical, dental, and vision plans, matching 401(k), unlimited PTO and paid holidays, parental/adoption leave, legal insurance, and a home technology stipend. Details of participation in these benefit plans will be provided when a candidate receives an offer of employment.
