jobs.title: Emergency Veterinary Assistant- Sandy, UT
jobs.description:
ABOUT VEG

In 2014, VEG was born with a mission to help people and their pets when they need it most. This meant challenging the status quo and fixing everything that was wrong with the ER experience. Since then, we’ve expanded rapidly, with hospitals nationwide open 24/7, 365 days a year, and created a better emergency experience—not only for people and their pets, but also for everyone who works here—our VEGgies!

At VEG we find a way to say yes to the career you want in veterinary emergency medicine. This means transforming how ER works, from our open-concept hospitals, where you can handle emergency cases of every kind (even exotics!) to our immersive, customer-focused experience, which helps us give people and their pets the care they deserve.

This also means saying yes to creating the best experience possible for our VEGgies. Yes to working in an environment where you can find your place and feel valued for the amazing work you do. Yes to having unparalleled opportunities for learning and mentorship so you can grow where you want to go in your career. And yes to making an impact here in ways you never thought possible.

VEG is a 2025 and 2026 certified Great Place to Work®.

THE JOB

At VEG, we don’t just hire assistants—we grow future emergency rockstars. As an Emergency Veterinary Assistant, you’ll be in the heart of the action from day one, supporting your team, comforting pet parents, and learning the ropes in real time. You’ll be there for everything—the triage, the treatments, and the tail wags. You’re embarking on a path where careers start, grow, and thrive. Whether you’re on your way to becoming a credentialed technician or exploring where your passion can take you, we’ll say yes to your growth every step of the way.

WHAT YOU’LL DO*

• Be the first warm welcome and a steady support, triaging incoming patients and helping guide them toward care

• Assist with treatments, nursing care, and diagnostics, from bloodwork and imaging to catheter placement and oxygen support

• Work alongside our credentialed veterinary technicians and veterinarians to set up and monitor anesthesia and sedation cases

• Set up and manage IV fluids, blood transfusions, and medication administration

• Assist during every moment of care: outpatient or inpatient, exam room to treatment area

• Join patient rounds and stay close to the clinical picture to ensure continuity of care

• Learn how to perform CPR and become a RECOVER Certified Rescuer (training provided!)

• Grow into more advanced responsibilities, such as anesthesia support, ultrasound, and catheterization through guided training pathways

*As permitted by state law

WHAT YOU NEED

• High school diploma or equivalent required

• Enrolled in an AVMA-accredited veterinary technology program a plus

• 1+ years in a veterinary assistant role (emergency or specialty experience is a bonus!)

• Basic computer skills and an understanding of practice management software and electronic medical record keeping

• Excellent communicator when collaborating with pet parents and your team

• Fine motor skills for handling patients and medical equipment

• Ability to stand for prolonged hours, kneel, and work on the floor as well as ability to lift up to 25 kg on own and able to support up to 40 kg with assistance

• Must be willing to work in a noisy environment with strong or unpleasant odors

• Availability to work nights, weekends, and holidays on a rotating or as needed basis based on hospital demands

• Ability to work well in a fast-paced environment with people from all backgrounds and different personality types

WHO YOU ARE

• Empathetic, instinctively taking a people-centric approach, whether supporting your colleagues or making an effort to understand different perspectives

• Have a sense of humility; acknowledging mistakes, sharing credit with others, and lifting up your team’s’ accomplishments

• Feel a strong sense of ownership over your work, taking responsibility for outcomes and staying committed to achieving long-term, impactful results

• Curious by nature; you ask insightful questions and continuously seek out opportunities to learn and grow your skills and knowledge

HOW WE INVEST IN YOU

• Competitive compensation, including base and 401K match

• Comprehensive health and wellness benefits that start on day one, including medical, dental, and vision coverage, QPR training, and access to free therapy or counseling

• Depending on your role, you may be eligible for equity after one year of full time, active employment with VEG, so you can share in our growth and success

• A BIG focus on learning and growth, from VEG-created clinical and leadership programs to unlimited ER CE + travel stipend (no really!). Full-time credentialed VEGgies receive a $2,500/year travel stipend. Full-time uncredentialed VEGgies receive a $1,000/year travel stipend.

• Clinical student loan repayment so you don’t need to worry about your student debt

• Paid parental leave; up to 12 weeks at 100% of regular salary and inclusive fertility and family-building care for all types of families

• Flexible work schedules to support your life outside of work

• Generous employee referral program, so our awesome people can bring in more awesome people

• And the little (big) things, like comfy scrubs, cool VEG swag, and food in the fridge for when you’re hungry

DEI

At VEG, diversity is not just a word—it's a strength that fuels innovation and kindness. Our mission is “Helping people and their pets when they need it most.” And we do that better when our VEGgies (employees) feel valued, respected, and empowered to bring their authentic selves to work. That's why we're devoted to creating an environment that reflects the diverse communities we serve—where different perspectives are not only welcomed but celebrated.

We are focused on providing equitable opportunities for growth, promoting inclusive decision-making, and ensuring that everyone's perspective is considered. Saying yes to VEG means helping us build a culture where your unique experiences and background contribute to a shared vision: being the world’s veterinary emergency company.

jobs.title: Domestic Abuse Victim Advocate (DAVA)
jobs.description:
Coho Integrated Solutions is seeking a qualified Domestic Abuse Victim Advocate (DAVA) to support the Department of the Air Force Family Advocacy Program in Eielson, Alaska. The DAVA provides advocacy, crisis intervention, safety planning, case management, resource coordination, and support to victims of domestic abuse.

The DAVA serves as a critical resource for victims and works closely with FAP clinicians, installation leadership, law enforcement, medical providers, and community agencies while maintaining the confidentiality and self-determination of victims within applicable program requirements.

Responsibilities (include but are not limited to):

• Provide 24-hour, seven-day-a-week response to victims alleging domestic abuse using the designated emergency contact process.

• Explain available advocacy services, reporting options, voluntary participation, and applicable confidentiality limitations to victims.

• Provide information regarding military and civilian resources, including protective orders, restraining orders, injunctions, legal services, medical resources, housing, childcare, and emergency shelter.

• Conduct approved risk assessments when evaluating the potential for imminent serious harm or death.

• Immediately notify appropriate FAP leadership, law enforcement, and command when imminent risk of serious harm or death is identified, in accordance with applicable procedures.

• Develop, implement, and regularly review individualized victim safety plans.

• Provide case management, follow-up, advocacy, information, referrals, and support based on victim needs and preferences.

• Empower victims in decision-making while supporting self-determination and informed choices.

• Accompany victims to medical appointments, court proceedings, and other authorized appointments when requested.

• Collaborate with FAP clinicians and mental health providers and provide relevant updates regarding victim circumstances and safety concerns.

• Support coordinated community response initiatives, system advocacy, education, and domestic abuse awareness.

• Establish and maintain partnerships with installation and local domestic abuse agencies and support resources.

Confidentiality and Professional Responsibilities:

• Maintain appropriate confidentiality and adhere to applicable victim advocacy requirements.

• Support victims without directing or making decisions on their behalf.

• Maintain communication with designated FAP and emergency contacts when providing advocacy services.

• Maintain accurate location, arrival, and departure information while providing victim advocacy services.

• Protect victim information and comply with applicable restrictions concerning Personal Health Information (PHI).

Essential Job Qualifications and Requirements:

• Clearance: Must be eligible for and maintain required privileging within the Military Treatment Facility Must be able to obtain and maintain a Public Trust determination in accordance with applicable contract and government requirements

• Education, Licensure, and Certifications: Must have a bachelor's degree from an accredited university Degree must be in Social Work, Psychology, Marriage/Family/Child Counseling, Counseling, Behavioral Science, Criminal Justice, or a related field Must possess or be able to obtain upon hire or within six months of hire the required Basic Advocate credential with the Comprehensive Intervention Specialist designation, as approved and offered through the National Advocate Credentialing Program overseen by the National Organization for Victim Assistance Basic Life Support (BLS) Certification

• Required Experience: Minimum of two years of experience assisting and providing advocacy services to victims of domestic abuse or sexual assault Demonstrated ability to provide crisis intervention, advocacy, safety planning, case management, and resource coordination

• Physical Requirements: Ability to respond to victims outside normal business hours as required. Ability to travel locally to medical appointments, court proceedings, and other approved locations Ability to work in office, clinical, community, and potentially crisis-oriented environments

• Work Environment: The DAVA works in a professional advocacy environment that may include offices, medical facilities, courts, community organizations, and other locations where victim support services are provided. The position requires flexibility and the ability to respond appropriately to sensitive and potentially urgent situations

jobs.title: Staff Product Manager, Radar - Fraud and Abuse Prevention
jobs.location: San Francisco, Seattle, New York, US-Remote
jobs.description:
About the team

Radar helps businesses prevent fraud and abuse without getting in the way of legitimate customers. We combine machine learning powered by Stripe’s global network with intuitive dashboard experiences and developer APIs, to give our users comprehensive controls and insights to protect their business against threats ranging from payment fraud and card testing to bot and free trial abuse.

Fraud doesn’t stand still, and it isn’t limited to checkout. As businesses launch new products and business models, attackers find new ways to exploit them. We obsess about understanding those attacks, identifying defenses that work, and making sophisticated fraud prevention simple for the businesses that depend on us to help them protect and grow their revenue with confidence.

What you’ll do

As a product manager on the Radar team, you’ll work directly with customers to understand the novel fraud and abuse attacks they face, identify the most important problems to solve, and turn those insights into product strategy and a roadmap.

You’ll work at the intersection of customers, engineering, data science, design, and commercial teams to shape what we build and bring it to market. Your work will span the fraud and abuse detection and control capabilities at the heart of Radar and the user and developer experiences that put those capabilities into our customers’ hands.

This role requires both urgency and taste. You’ll move quickly as threats evolve, without compromising on reliability, craft, or the details that make complex products feel beautifully simple.

Responsibilities

• Develop a deep understanding of the fraud and abuse landscape.

• Investigate emerging attacks with customers, assess their financial and operational impact, and distinguish isolated incidents from opportunities to build broadly useful defenses.

• Translate findings into a product strategy and roadmap, prioritizing the defenses that deliver the greatest customer and business impact.

• Partner with engineering, data science, and design to explore signals, shape solutions, and rapidly turn effective defenses into scalable, reliable products.

• Set the pace for the team by scoping the product thoughtfully, prioritizing ruthlessly, and executing with high rigor.

• Work with sales, marketing, and customer-facing teams to validate demand, coordinate launches, and help customers adopt and maximize the value they get from new capabilities.

• Own product performance, user experience, and business metrics to guide iteration and communicate progress.

Who you are

We’re looking for someone who meets the minimum requirements to be considered for the role. If you meet these requirements, you are encouraged to apply. The preferred qualifications are a bonus, not a requirement.

Minimum requirements

• 10+ years of Product Management experience

• Highly analytical, with a rigorous approach to quantitative and qualitative evidence. You’re comfortable digging into data, writing SQL when needed, and defining metrics that connect product decisions to user outcomes.

• Scrappy and resourceful, with experience taking products from zero to one. You find ways to test ideas quickly, learn from real users, and turn early solutions into products that scale.

• Strong commercial and business acumen. You understand how customer problems translate into willingness to pay, adoption, and durable business value.

• Proven cross-functional leadership, including experience partnering with B2B sales teams on customer discovery, product positioning, and adoption.

• Experience shipping Dashboard and API products, with empathy for both end users and developers and an understanding of their different workflows.

• Comfort with substantial ambiguity. You can set direction with incomplete information, make thoughtful trade-offs, and adapt as new evidence emerges.

• Technical fluency to go deep with engineering and data teams on complex systems, understand constraints, and evaluate alternative approaches.

• Strong written and verbal communication skills, with a talent for distilling complex customer problems into precise, actionable framing.

• An ownership mindset and a high bar for product quality. You do what it takes to solve user problems and care deeply about the details of the experience.

Preferred qualifications

• Experience building fraud, abuse prevention, risk, or security products.

• Experience developing machine learning powered products and evaluating trade-offs between detection effectiveness and customer friction.

• Experience building tools for fraud analysts or risk teams, or developer products that support real-time decisions.

• Software engineering, data science, or similar technical experience.

jobs.description:
This position is on behalf of Mass Mentoring: Affiliate of MENTOR

Position Title: Institutional Giving Manager
Reports to: Director of Development
Department: Advancement
Classification: Exempt - Full Time
Working Hours: Standard hours with night and weekend hours expected for special events
Working Location: Hybrid Boston - Majority onsite in Boston-based office, with some remote flexibility and statewide travel
Salary: $70,000 - $75,000 year (commensurate with experience)
Application Submission Deadline: Applications will be reviewed on a rolling basis until the position is filled
Anticipated Start Date: ASAP

Organizational Overview:
Mass Mentoring Partnership (MMP) is a dynamic statewide nonprofit organization committed to ensuring that every young person in MA has access to quality mentoring relationships, regardless of who they are or where they live.
An affiliate of The National Mentoring Partnership (MENTOR), MMP is part of a national effort that helps grassroots organizations foster quality mentoring relationships by producing research for the field, shaping policy change through advocacy, and driving public awareness on the impact of mentoring for young people.
For more than 30 years MMP has served as an intermediary organization, providing the critical link between national evidence-based research and programs across Massachusetts. MMP provides the tools, research, training, and best practices adults require to truly show up for youth in a caring and consistent way in schools, community, and workplaces.
We are committed to fostering an environment of diversity, equity, inclusion and belonging for all. We embrace our differences and celebrate our common humanity by valuing our varied perspectives, experiences, and opinions. Candidates of color, bilingual, and bicultural candidates are strongly encouraged to apply.

Position Summary:
Mass Mentoring Partnership (MMP) is seeking a strategic, relationship-driven Institutional Giving Manager to lead and grow the organization's foundation, corporate, and government fundraising portfolio.

Reporting to the Director of Development, the Institutional Giving Manager will be responsible for cultivating institutional funders, developing compelling proposals, stewarding existing partners, and identifying new funding opportunities that advance MMP's mission. This position plays a critical role in securing philanthropic investments that strengthen mentoring and youth-serving organizations across Massachusetts; helping meet MMP’s annual revenue goal of $2.5 million.

The successful candidate is an exceptional relationship builder and strategic thinker who is energized by building connections across the philanthropic, corporate, and community landscape. This role requires an active external presence—representing MMP at events, networking opportunities, and community gatherings to cultivate relationships and expand the organization's institutional funding pipeline.

Key Responsibilities:

Institutional Fundraising
● Develop and implement an annual strategy to grow foundation, corporate, and government revenue.

● Manage a portfolio of institutional funders through all stages of the fundraising cycle, including identification, cultivation, solicitation, stewardship, and renewal.

● Represent MMP externally by attending philanthropic, corporate, and community events; cultivate new relationships and identify opportunities that strengthen the institutional giving pipeline.

● Research and identify prospective funders aligned with MMP's mission and strategic priorities.

● Build and maintain relationships with foundation program officers, corporate giving representatives, and public-sector funders.

Proposal Development

● Write compelling letters of inquiry, grant proposals, sponsorship proposals, reports, and supporting materials.

● Ethically and responsibly use AI-enabled tools to enhance research, content development, and
administrative efficiency while maintaining quality, accuracy, and originality of all work products.

● Partner with program staff to gather outcomes, budgets, stories, and evaluation data.

● Ensure all submissions accurately reflect organizational priorities and measurable impact.

Stewardship & Reporting

● Manage grant reporting schedules and ensure timely submission of all required reports.

● Develop stewardship plans that deepen relationships with institutional supporters.

● Coordinate site visits, meetings, presentations, and funder communications.

Corporate Partnerships

● Cultivate corporate partnerships and sponsorship opportunities by building relationships with business leaders, attending relevant networking events, and identifying opportunities to align corporate priorities with MMP's mission.

● Develop customized partnership proposals that align business objectives with MMP's mission.

● Work collaboratively with the Director of Development to grow long-term corporate relationships.

Strategy & Analysis

● Maintain a comprehensive grants calendar and institutional fundraising pipeline.

● Track proposal activity, deadlines, awards, and reporting requirements.

● Analyze fundraising performance and identify opportunities for portfolio growth.

● Monitor trends in philanthropy, education, workforce development, mentoring, and youth development.

Cross-Functional Collaboration

● Collaborate with the Development Communications Specialist to develop compelling case statements, impact reports, and donor communications.

● Partner with the Manager of Development Operations to maintain accurate donor and gift records in the CRM and ensure timely, accurate gift acknowledgments and thank-you letters.

● Coordinate with program staff to translate organizational impact into persuasive funding opportunities.

● Assist in the planning and execution of fundraising and engagement events, including Cheers to Mentoring, Mentoring Night at Fenway, the Business Community Breakfast, and other special events; partner with the Director of Development to create and market sponsorship opportunities.

● Assist with organizational fundraising initiatives as needed

CORE COMPETENCIES & QUALIFICATIONS

● Bachelors Degree in relevant field with 4 years of experience or a Master’s Degree in relevant field with 2 years experience preferred. Can be supplemented with: Minimum of 8 - 10 years of experience in Nonprofit development.

● Demonstrated success securing five and six-figure foundation, corporate, and/or government grants.

● Exceptional writing, editing, and storytelling skills.

● Strong project management with the ability to manage multiple deadlines simultaneously.

● Experience developing proposal budgets and grant reports.

● Strong interpersonal and relationship-building skills.

● Experience using donor databases or CRM systems (Salesforce).

● Knowledge of and passion for advancing equity in youth development, education, mentoring, and workforce development sectors.

● Experience with statewide or intermediary nonprofit organizations.

● Familiarity with Massachusetts philanthropic and corporate giving landscape.

● Familiarity with AI-powered productivity tools (e.g., Google Gemini, ChatGPT, Grammarly AI) and the ability to use them ethically and effectively to support fundraising.

Benefits:

● Salary $70,000 - $75,000/year - paid biweekly (commensurate with experience)

● Health & Dental insurance with employer premium contribution of 70% of monthly premium

● Paid time off including 13 paid holidays (plus 4 floating holiday)

● 401k with employer match (up to 4%)

● Life and STD/LTD insurance premiums 100% employer funded

● Pre-Tax Commuter Benefit

● Section 125 Flexible Benefit Plan

● Employee Assistance Program (EAP)

● Professional Development funds available

● Hybrid work environment (2 set days a week in-person per week) at MMP’s new centrally located office in the heart of downtown crossing, half a block from red, orange, and green lines

Next Steps: Please email a resume and cover letter (or link to video cover letter) that outlines how your skills and experiences meet the qualifications of the position, stating how you heard about this opportunity to Jill Precopio, Director of Development at humanresources@massmentors.org with the subject line: Institutional Giving Manager. Applications are accepted on a rolling basis (applications without a cover letter will not be considered). Please note that due to the high volume of applications we receive, we are unable to respond to each applicant individually. Mass Mentoring Partnership provides equal employment opportunities for all applicants and employees. All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to sex, gender identity, gender expression, sexual orientation, race, color, religion, national origin, disability, protected Veteran status, age, or any other characteristic protected by applicable law.

We are committed to building a team that represents a variety of backgrounds, perspectives, and skills. The more inclusive we are, the better our work will be. Mass Mentoring Partnership is committed to the full inclusion of all qualified individuals. As part of this commitment, MMP will ensure that persons with disabilities are provided reasonable accommodations. If reasonable accommodation is needed to participate in the job application or interview process, to perform essential job functions, and/or to receive other benefits and privileges of employment, please contact humanresources@massmentors.org.

jobs.title: Technical Release Specialist
jobs.description:
THE POSITION
Our roster has an opening with your name on it

The Technical Release Specialist oversees the end-to-end release lifecycle, ensuring that software deployments are delivered reliably, efficiently, and with minimal risk. This role acts as the central coordinator across engineering, QA, product, and operations, driving standardized processes that improve release quality and accelerate time to market.

In addition to the specific responsibilities outlined above, employees may be required to perform other such duties as assigned by the Company. This ensures operational flexibility and allows the Company to meet evolving business needs.

THE GAME PLAN
Everyone on our team has a part to play

• Establish and maintain consistent, repeatable deployment practices to reduce risk and improve quality.

• Implement structured release workflows that reduce production outages and business disruption.

• Serve as the central point of communication, aligning engineering, QA, product, and operations to prevent bottlenecks and duplicate work.

• Streamline approvals and release workflows to improve time to market new features and updates.

• Oversee comprehensive testing, validation, and risk assessments to prevent errors and protect customer experience.

• Provide day-to-day support for release management inquiries and requests.

• Manage sandbox creation, updates, and general upkeep to support development and QA activities.

• Strong presentation and documentation skills

FanDuel Group consists of a portfolio of leading brands across mobile wagering including: America’s #1 Sportsbook, FanDuel Sportsbook; its leading iGaming platform, FanDuel Casino; the industry’s unquestioned leader in horse racing and advance-deposit wagering, FanDuel Racing; and its daily fantasy sports product.

In addition, FanDuel Group operates FanDuel TV, its broadly distributed linear cable television network and FanDuel TV+, its leading direct-to-consumer OTT platform. FanDuel Group has a presence across all 50 states, Canada, and Puerto Rico.

The company is based in New York with US offices in Los Angeles, Atlanta, and Jersey City, as well as global offices in Canada and Scotland. The company’s affiliates have offices worldwide, including in Ireland, Portugal, Romania, and Australia.

FanDuel Group is a subsidiary of Flutter Entertainment, the world's largest sports betting and gaming operator with a portfolio of globally recognized brands and traded on the New York Stock Exchange (NYSE: FLUT).

We treat our team right

We offer amazing benefits above and beyond the basics. We have an array of health plans to choose from (some as low as $0 per paycheck) that include programs for fertility and family planning, mental health support, and fitness benefits. We offer generous paid time off (PTO & sick leave), annual bonus and long-term incentive opportunities (based on performance), 401k with up to a 5% match, commuter benefits, pet insurance, and more - check out all our benefits here: FanDuel Total Rewards. *Benefits differ across location, role, and level.

As such, we are committed to equal employment opportunity regardless of race, color, ethnicity, ancestry, religion, creed, sex, national origin, sexual orientation, age, citizenship status, marital status, disability, gender identity, gender expression, veteran status, or any other characteristic protected by state, local or federal law. If you have a disability and need a workplace accommodation or adjustment during the application and hiring process, including support for the interview or onboarding process, please email Benefits@fanduel.com.

jobs.title: Customer data specialist, US (fixed-term)
jobs.description:
ABOUT WATERSHED

Watershed https://watershed.com/ is the enterprise sustainability platform. Companies like Airbnb, Carlyle Group, FedEx, Visa, and Dr. Martens use Watershed to manage climate and ESG data, produce audit-ready metrics for voluntary and regulatory reporting including CSRD, and drive real decarbonization. We are looking for team members who love product-building, want to work hard at a mission-oriented startup, and will collaborate with us in shaping the culture of a growing team.



We have offices in San Francisco, New York, Denver, London, Paris, Berlin, Sydney, Mexico City, and remote team members across the US and Europe. We hope that you'll be interested in joining us!




THE ROLE

We are looking for analytically minded and detail-oriented individuals to join the Customer Data Services team in our New York or San Francisco office on a fixed-term basis starting at the beginning of January 2027. This role is open to early-career candidates with up to 2 years of experience who love working with complex data and want to see how it drives real decisions at the world's largest companies.

 

Watershed is a growth-stage start-up that works with 800+ customers globally, including 100+ of the Fortune 500 and 5 of the top 6 US banks, to accelerate their sustainability programs. You'll work hands-on with customer business data, transforming it to fit Watershed templates and enabling our customers to gain clear, reliable insights into their sustainability impact.



YOU WILL

 - Clean and transform customer business data into Watershed templates to reduce customer friction and drive time-to-value.

 - Partner with customers to understand their raw data and recommend best practices for preparing it.

 - Communicate data issues clearly to customers, covering impact, options and trade-offs.

 - Leverage judgment to assess, advise, and execute on data cleaning best practices.

 - Rigorously document decisions to ensure traceability of data manipulations during third-party verifications.

 - Synthesize customer experiences and feedback to drive continuous improvement of our work and inform product development.



YOU MIGHT BE A FIT IF YOU

 - Have up to 2 years of experience working with large data files in Excel, whether through internships, co-ops or academic projects. Python or SQL is a plus.

 - Thrive on complex, messy data and enjoy the work of making it clean, structured, and trustworthy.

 - Are detail obsessed. You double check your work and do not consider something done until you know it is right.

 - Have good intuition for how numbers in a spreadsheet map to the real world. You translate abstract problems into concrete data frameworks.

 - Have high customer empathy and want to help them achieve their outcomes.

 - Are a strong written and verbal communicator. You can concisely communicate externally to non-technical audiences.

 - Are a low ego team player with a strong sense of ownership. You are driven by team goals and bias for action in order to achieve them.



FIXED-TERM DETAILS

 - Minimum commitment of 4 months, with a possible extension of up to 3 additional months.

 - Fixed-term employees receive compensation and benefits similar to full-time Watershed employees, including daily lunch delivered in the Watershed office.

 - This position requires being in person in our San Francisco or New York office 4 days per week.

   





   

Must be willing to work from an office 4 days per week (except for remote roles)

Watershed has hub offices in San Francisco, New York, London, and Mexico City and satellite offices in Denver, Sydney, Paris, and Berlin. Where we have offices, employees are expected to be in office for 4 days per week. Certain jobs are open to being remote and will be specifically noted on the jobs page and in the job description if so.



What’s the interview process like?

It starts the same for every candidate: getting to know the team members through 1 to 2 conversations about Watershed, your experience, and your interests. Next steps can vary by role, but usual next steps are a skill or experience interview (e.g. a coding interview for an engineer, a portfolio review for a designer, deeper experience call for other roles) which leads to a virtual or in person interview panel. We prioritize transparency and lack of surprise throughout the process.



What if I need accommodations for my interview?

At Watershed, we are dedicated to ensuring an inclusive recruitment process. We provide reasonable accommodations for candidates with disabilities, long-term conditions, mental health needs, religious observances, neurodivergence, or pregnancy-related support requirements. If you need assistance during your process, please contact your recruiter.

jobs.title: Product Manager, Radar
jobs.location: San Francisco, Seattle, New York, US-Remote
jobs.description:
About the team

Radar helps businesses prevent fraud and abuse without getting in the way of legitimate customers. We combine machine learning powered by Stripe’s global network with intuitive dashboard experiences and developer APIs, to give our users comprehensive controls and insights to protect their business against threats ranging from payment fraud and card testing to bot and free trial abuse.

Fraud doesn’t stand still, and it isn’t limited to checkout. As businesses launch new products and business models, attackers find new ways to exploit them. We obsess about understanding those attacks, identifying defenses that work, and making sophisticated fraud prevention simple for the businesses that depend on us to help them protect and grow their revenue with confidence.

What you’ll do

As a product manager on the Radar team, you’ll help customers, developers, and partners bring fraud prevention naturally into the systems and workflows they rely on. You’ll shape products that make fraud management feel effortless, connecting Radar’s capabilities to the tools and experiences our users build and run.

You’ll work at the intersection of customer needs and commercial opportunities to shape what we build and how we bring it to market. Working closely with engineering, data science, design, and go-to-market teams, you’ll build products and relationships that deliver lasting value to customers and partners. You’ll connect technical decisions to commercial outcomes while maintaining a high bar for reliability, craft, and the details that make complex products feel simple.

Responsibilities

• Develop a deep understanding of the payments and fraud landscape, how businesses manage risk, and the systems and workflows they rely on.

• Work directly with customers, developers, and partners to uncover unmet needs, understand integration challenges, and identify opportunities to build broadly useful products.

• Develop and communicate a clear product strategy and roadmap, prioritizing opportunities based on user impact, technical feasibility, and business value.

• Partner closely with engineering and data science to turn sophisticated fraud control and monitoring capabilities into reliable APIs, intuitive tools, and well-crafted developer experiences.

• Drive product development from ideation through launch, setting the pace, scoping thoughtfully, prioritizing ruthlessly, and executing with rigor.

• Collaborate deeply with sales, marketing, and partnerships teams to identify opportunities, validate demand, and drive the adoption of new experiences.

• Work with customers and partners through early implementations, using hands-on feedback to improve documentation, onboarding, and the path from initial evaluation to production use.

• Own metrics for integration success, adoption, retention, revenue, and user value; use results to guide product and commercial decisions and communicate progress.

• Communicate clearly with internal and external stakeholders about priorities, trade-offs, progress, and results, building alignment across teams you don’t directly manage.

Who you are

We’re looking for someone who meets the minimum requirements to be considered for the role. If you meet these requirements, you are encouraged to apply. The preferred qualifications are a bonus, not a requirement.

Minimum requirements

• 8+ years of Product Management experience

• Highly analytical, with a rigorous approach to quantitative and qualitative evidence. You’re comfortable digging into data, writing SQL when needed, and connecting product decisions to user and business outcomes.

• Scrappy and resourceful, with experience taking products from zero to one. You thrive in early-stage environments, test ideas quickly, and turn what you learn into products that scale.

• Strong commercial and business acumen. You understand how customer needs, market dynamics, and product differentiation translate into adoption and durable business value.

• Proven cross-functional leadership, including experience partnering with B2B sales teams on customer discovery, technical evaluation, and commercialization.

• Experience shipping Dashboard and API products, with empathy for end users and developers alike.

• Experience developing pricing and monetization models for B2B products.

• Technical fluency to go deep with engineers on APIs, system architecture, and integration trade-offs, and to explain those decisions clearly to customers.

• Strong written and verbal communication skills, with a talent for distilling complex user problems into precise, actionable framing.

• An ownership mindset and a high bar for product quality. You do what it takes to solve user problems and care deeply about the details of the experience.

Preferred qualifications

• Experience building payments, fraud prevention, risk, or security products.

• Experience building developer platforms and working with integration partners, including navigating technical dependencies and high-stakes external relationships.

jobs.title: Engineering Manager (Embedded)
jobs.description:
DS creates systems that power the next generation of radio spectrum intelligence. We collect radio data from all over the world, train neural networks to decipher it, and run them on the smallest chips we can. We’re solving a new, technically hard problem where nothing from other fields works out of the box, and along the way, we’ve built our own stack from scratch, including entirely new embedding model architectures, custom GPU kernels, and much more.

Joining DS means owning major parts of a fast-growing AI research organization, joining a collaborative, talent-dense team with decades of experience in probabilistic ML, accelerated computing, embedded systems, and signal theory, and growing your career in the areas that interest you. You’ll fit in if you want to come to work for the problem itself and don’t want to choose between technical rigor, business value, and real-world impact. 

We work with high ownership and trust.




THE ROLE

We are hiring an Engineering Manager (Embedded) to lead the team that builds the software running on our sensors. This is the team accountable for everything that happens on the device: the embedded Linux platform, the interfaces to our hardware, the runtime that executes our models on the smallest chips we can, and the reliability of every unit we have deployed in the field.

This is a people-leader-first, technically-deep role. You are not expected to be writing production code day to day. You are expected to be technical enough to own the architecture alongside your team, review a design and find the thing that will break in the field, hold a line on a decision about memory, timing, or hardware interaction, and be trusted by your engineers as a technical peer rather than a coordinator.

Our product operates where embedded systems, machine learning, and hardware meet the real world. Decisions about memory, power, thermal budget, timing, and connectivity surface directly in what the customer experiences. There is no clean separation between the device and the product, and the constraints of the sensor are the constraints of the business. This is an on-site role with our in-person NYC team.



WHAT YOU'LL OWN

 - The embedded and edge software platform: embedded Linux, the build and image toolchain, service orchestration, and the software running on every sensor we ship

 - The hardware and software boundary: board bring-up, driver and interface work, and the path from a new hardware revision to shipping software

 - On-sensor model deployment: the runtime, tooling, and pipeline that get our models onto constrained compute and keep them fast

 - Field and deployment reliability: OTA updates, fleet health, and what actually happens on hardware nobody can physically touch

 - The embedded roadmap and its execution, tied to annual company goals

 - A team of embedded software engineers you will coach, develop, and hire


HOW YOU'LL LEAD

 - Own the roadmap and delivery for embedded, and turn broad direction into clear objectives your team can execute against

 - Hold the technical bar: review architecture, ask the question nobody else is asking, and surface the right tradeoffs to our Head of Engineering.

 - Coach engineers on technical judgment and ownership, not just execution

 - Hire and interview embedded and systems engineers as the team grows

 - Partner with ML, RF, hardware, and mission operations so the device, the model, and the customer deployment stay in sync

 - Own company goals and drive execution through ambiguity


WHAT SUCCESS LOOKS LIKE

 - Software that behaves predictably on hardware in the field, under real power, thermal, and connectivity constraints

 - A shorter, more repeatable path from a new hardware revision to shipping software

 - Updates that reach deployed sensors without a person on site and without anyone holding their breath

 - Engineers who are growing in technical judgment and ownership

 - Embedded decisions that hold up as the fleet, the team, and the product grow



ABOUT YOU

You are someone who:

 - Has led embedded, firmware, or systems engineers, and wants to keep leading them

 - Came up as a strong embedded or systems engineer and never lost the instinct

 - Thinks in systems, not just frameworks, and knows how the OS, memory, hardware, and network interact

 - Can hold a technical position with a senior engineer without writing the code yourself

 - Has shipped software onto hardware that lives somewhere you cannot reach

 - Is comfortable with hardware timelines, board revisions, and problems that are still bein defined

 - Is eligible for a United States Security Clearance



TECHNICAL BACKGROUND

You've worked meaningfully with:

 - Embedded Linux (kernel space and user space) or real time operating systems

 - C, C++, and Python

 - Yocto, Buildroot, or other embedded Linux toolchains

 - Docker, systemd, or other service orchestration mechanisms

 - IP networking fundamentals and system-level debugging on constrained devices

 - Communication protocols such as SPI, I2C, UART, and Ethernet

 - Build systems, packaging, OTA and deployment, and CI/CD for hardware targets

You understand:

 - How hardware and software interact in embedded systems, and how to run that boundary with a hardware team

 - How systems fail under memory, power, thermal, and networking pressure

 - How to design software that cannot assume constant connectivity

 - What it takes to update, debug, and trust a fleet you cannot physically touch



NICE-TO-HAVES

 - Experience with software that takes advantage of hardware accelerators (FPGA, DSP, GPU)

 - Experience deploying machine learning models to constrained edge compute

 - Familiarity with Rust, Golang, or Systemverilog

 - Familiarity with the fundamentals of signal processing, machine learning, computer vision, or related disciplines

 - Experience with Electronic Warfare Systems, Radar, Software Defined Radio, or related domains

 - Possession of a US Secret or higher clearance



THIS ROLE IS LIKELY NOT FOR YOU IF...

 - You want to stay a full-time individual contributor

 - Your leadership experience is entirely in cloud or application software and embedded constraints would be new to you

 - You have managed embedded teams as a coordinator without owning technical direction

 - You need a stable hardware platform and a finished roadmap to manage against

 - You prefer narrowly scoped ownership over end-to-end responsibility

 - You are uncomfortable leading in environments where the problem is still being defined


WHO THRIVES AT DISTRIBUTED SPECTRUM 

 - Fast learners over specific backgrounds – We care more about how quickly you can pick up new skills than where you’ve worked before.

 - Intellectual honesty – The right answer matters more than being right. You challenge assumptions, test ideas, and pivot when needed.

 - Adaptability – We’re organized, but sometimes things change quickly. You find a way to make it work and balance short-term deliverables with long-term goals.

 - Ownership of outcomes – You optimize your own time, focus on what matters to deliver quickly, and cut out inefficiencies.

 - Not building in a vacuum – You stay connected to the rest of our teams and our customers to make sure all the pieces fit together.




WHAT WE OFFER 

 - Above-market salary, equity, and benefits package. 

 - Early Series A Equity

 - Excellent health, dental, and vision coverage

 - 401(k) match - up to 4% of your salary

 - Flexible PTO

 - Daily office lunches in NYC



ITAR Requirements

To conform to U.S. Government technology export regulations, including the International Traffic in Arms Regulations (ITAR) you must be a U.S. citizen, lawful permanent resident of the U.S., protected individual as defined by 8 U.S.C. 1324b(a)(3), or eligible to obtain the required authorizations from the U.S. Department of State. Learn more about the ITAR here https://www.pmddtc.state.gov/?id=ddtc_kb_article_page&sys_id=24d528fddbfc930044f9ff621f961987.

jobs.title: Partner Engagement Manager, Army Command and General Staff College
jobs.description:
CONSEQUENTIAL WORK. DEDICATED PEOPLE.



ABOUT ONEBRIEF


Onebrief builds collaboration and AI-powered workflow software for military planning and operational coordination.

Military planning is complex by nature, requiring teams to coordinate information, people, and decisions across systems and locations. Onebrief brings planning, collaboration, simulation, and AI into one connected environment, helping teams test strategies, adapt to changing conditions, and make decisions with greater clarity when the stakes are real.

We are a distributed team of builders from military, operational, and technology backgrounds who care deeply about improving how important work gets done. Some team members work remotely, while others work directly alongside customers in operational environments around the world.

Founded in 2019, Onebrief is backed by leading investors including General Catalyst, Battery Ventures, Insight Partners, Sapphire Ventures, and Human Capital. Valued at more than $2 billion, we continue to invest in product innovation, AI capabilities, and team growth.

Required: Top Secret clearance with eligibility for SCI

In person in Fort Leavenworth, KS




WHY THIS ROLE EXISTS

As a Partner Engagement Manager at Onebrief, you're the customer's trusted technical partner. You serve as the subject-matter expert, maintaining power-user-level fluency in the platform. You stay current on product updates, translating new releases into practical impact for the specific workflows your customer relies on. You act as the primary line of communication between the customer and Onebrief — as the product evolves, you deliver ongoing, role-specific training to ensure users adopt new capabilities rather than getting stuck on outdated workflows. You bridge the technical gap between engineering and the customer, explaining product behavior in terms their staff can actually act on.




WHAT YOU’LL DO

Core responsibilities:

 - Support students through in-classroom implementation and planning exercises.

 - Identify gaps between existing academic staff workflows and effective Onebrief usage, then drive adoption through hands-on configuration, user coaching, and workflow optimization**.**

 - Understand, request, and effectively leverage Company resources to meet the goals of the Company.

 - Clearly communicate user needs to the product team. Maintain a high product proficiency, and excite the customer about each product improvement.

 - Use your observations of our users to recommend product improvements.

 - When responding to incidents (product is unavailable, broken, or not delighting the customer), coordinate with the customer and our product engineering team.

 - Align your team’s efforts to deliver the best customer experience, while coordinating with fellow Partner Engagement Managers to ensure planning and workflows remain synchronized across commands.

 - Enable expansion and upsell opportunities to students from other Joint Services as well as Allies and Partners by instilling the Onebrief value proposition.

 - Be available to travel ~25% of the time to support other accounts in the region, when required.




MINIMUM QUALIFICATIONS

 - Proven experience in leading operational planning within a military context, preferably in a multi-star headquarters and instructional experience in Professional Military Education.

 - Familiarity and experience with major military planning exercises and the protocols for software deployment on government networks.

 - Proven ability to expand business presence within a customer location with emphasis on software or technology solutions.

 - Experience in customer support, both face-to-face and remote, and capability to respond to incidents coordinating with customers and product engineering teams.

 - Strong technical skills to master our platform, troubleshoot issues and liaise with customers on technical matters.

 - Proven ability to navigate large government organizations, solve bureaucratic challenges, and deliver successful outcomes.

 - You hold a current Top Secret clearance with eligibility for SCI and have the ability to access DOD facilities and installations.




PREFERRED QUALIFICATIONS

 - You’re technically adept. You don’t need to code, but you do need to be savvy. Can you become a power user of our product and talk engineering with the customer?

 - Customers trust you. You demonstrate strong interpersonal skills, develop rapport, align diverse perspectives, and communicate with clarity and influence.

 - You’re intense about our mission. It’s a core part of who you are

 - You’re proactive and adaptable. You see a problem and get to work. You’re comfortable working autonomously or in a cross-functional team, especially in a fast-paced or ambiguous setting

 - You communicate clearly, concisely, and candidly. Our Company relies on you to assess the situation within your account and effectively communicate your assessment and recommendations to inform strategic decisions.




INDICATORS OF SUCCESS

This role will evolve as priorities change, but the outcomes below reflect what success typically looks like in the first six months.

A successful Partner Engagement Manager will:

 - Opinion and expertise are valued by the customer and company alike (rapport/trust)

 - Learns quick, identifies opportunities and drives progress within the account (forward-leaning/ bias for action)

 - Open-minded and able to pivot when priorities shift (adaptability/humility)

In the absence of an executed Recruitment Services Agreement, there will be no obligation to any referral compensation or recruiter fee. In the event a recruiter or agency submits a resume or candidate without an agreement Onebrief explicitly reserves the right to pursue and hire those candidate(s) without any financial obligation to the recruiter or agency. jobs.description:
DLR Group is an integrated design firm with a promise to elevate the human experience through design. This fuels the work we do around the world and inspires our mission to improve the lives of our clients, our communities, and our planet. If this sparks your interest, you’re in the right place.

Our Information Technology team is growing. We're searching for an Entry-Level Service Desk Analyst to join our Seattle studio.

Position Summary

We’re looking for a skilled and service-oriented IT professional to join our team as a Service Desk Analyst. In this role, you will provide responsive, customer-focused technical support to employees across the firm. You will troubleshoot hardware, software, connectivity, and system issues; support company devices and peripherals; and help ensure employees have reliable access to the technology they need to work effectively. This role is ideal for a service-minded IT professional who enjoys solving problems, communicating with users, and working in a collaborative, fast-paced environment.

What you will do

• Respond to technical support requests by phone, service desk ticket, email, and in-person support

• Troubleshoot and resolve hardware, software, connectivity, and peripheral issues using diagnostic and remote support tools

• Provide local on-site technical support and remote assistance to employees across multiple DLR Group locations

• Install, configure, test, maintain, and troubleshoot laptops, desktops, printers, peripherals, and other IT-related equipment

• Support commonly used business applications, including Microsoft Windows, Microsoft Office, Adobe Creative Suite, and Google applications

• Document issues, troubleshooting steps, user communication, and resolutions within the service desk management system

• Prioritize, assign, and escalate support requests appropriately based on urgency, complexity, and area of responsibility

• Manage and track hardware assets to maintain accurate inventory, availability, and lifecycle information

• Provide guidance and training to employees and fellow team members on technology, computer operations, and common support issues

• Develop and maintain knowledge base articles, FAQs, and technical documentation to improve user support and knowledge sharing

Required Qualifications:

• 2–3 years of experience in information technology, service desk support, systems administration, or a related technical support role

• Education or training in Computer Science, Management Information Systems, Information Technology, or a related field

• Ability to travel regionally 1-2 times a month

• Experience troubleshooting laptops, desktops, printers, peripherals, and other business technology

• Experience supporting Microsoft Windows, Microsoft Office, Adobe Creative Suite, Google applications, or similar enterprise software

• Experience using service desk, ticketing, diagnostic, or remote assistance tools

• Ability to research technical issues and use technical manuals, procedural documentation, and manufacturer resources to identify solutions

• Strong analytical and troubleshooting skills with close attention to detail

• Strong customer service, interpersonal, written, and verbal communication skills

• Ability to communicate technical information clearly to users with varying levels of technical knowledge

• Ability to prioritize multiple requests and work effectively in a collaborative, fast-paced environment

Preferred Qualifications:

• Bachelor’s degree in Computer Science, Management Information Systems, Information Technology, or a related field

• Relevant technical certifications

• Experience providing IT support within a multi-office or geographically distributed organization

• Experience with hardware asset management and lifecycle tracking

• Experience developing technical documentation, knowledge base articles, or user-facing support resources

• Experience supporting multifunction printers, large-format printers, copiers, and other specialized office equipment

• Experience working across multiple IT functional areas and coordinating escalations with specialized technical teams

• Experience providing technical training or guidance to end users

Applicants must be legally authorized to work in the United States. We are unable to sponsor or take over sponsorship of a school/employment or any other visa, regardless of expiration date, now or in the future.

#LI-MIS

Our comprehensive Benefits at DLR Group include medical, dental, vision, disability, wellness programs, flex spending, paid holidays, and paid time off. We also offer a 401(k) plan, employee stock ownership, and bonus opportunities. Compensation considerations are based on location, experience, and skills. The suggested hourly rate for this position is:

Hourly Rate

$32.70—$35.10 USD

DLR Group is an integrated design firm delivering architecture, engineering, interiors, planning, and building optimization for new builds, renovations, and adaptive reuse projects.

We are 100% employee-owned: every employee is literally invested in our clients’ success. At the core of our firm are interdisciplinary teams engaged in every step of project lifecycles. Our teams champion true collaboration, open information sharing, shared risk and reward, value-based decision making, and proficient use of technology to deliver exceptional design. We are pursuing the goals of the 2030 Challenge, the ME2040, and the SE2050, and are an initial signatory of the China Accord and the AIA 2030 Commitment.

Through our values – commitment, creativity, environmental stewardship, fun, integrity, ownership, sharing, teamwork – we elevate the human experience through design, together.

DLR Group follows a four-day in-office work model, with employees having the flexibility to work somewhere other than the office on Fridays.

We are proud to be an Equal Opportunity/Affirmative Action/M/F/Veteran/Disabled employer.

jobs.title: Sexual Assault Nurse Examiner RN-Casual Rotating Shifts
jobs.description:
Internal Applicants Notice: Should you be seeking dual employment, please know this would be a casual status position with the casual status pay that is equivalent to the standard nursing pay at NM, not the IHR rate that is advertised.

The Sexual Assault Nurse Examiner (SANE) reflects the mission, vision, and values of NM, adheres to the organization’s Code of Ethics and Corporate Compliance Program, and complies with all relevant policies, procedures, guidelines and all other regulatory and accreditation standards.

• The SANE (Sexual Assault Nurse Examiner) is a registered professional nurse who provides exemplary specialized, trauma-informed medical forensic services to all individuals who presents with a complaint or concern of sexual assault. These services will be prompt, non-judgmental and compassionate while encouraging autonomy and reducing psychological trauma. The medical forensic services may include a medical forensic exam and evidence collection, counseling for emergency contraception, prophylactic treatment for sexually transmitted infections, photo documentation, and referrals for appropriate medical and psychological follow-up, support and participation in legal proceedings.

Responsibilities:

• Acts autonomously following the professional standards as outlined by the Sexual Assault Survivors Emergency Treatment Act (SASETA), the Illinois Nurse Practice Act, the International Association of Forensic Nurses Scope and Standards of Practice, and unit specific protocols appropriate to the patient population served.
• Works collaboratively with the interdisciplinary team, including SANE coordinator, providers, imaging and therapeutic services to facilitate care of sexual assault survivor.
• Maintains documentation standards with accurate, timely and complete recording and reporting to ensure compliance with SASETA.
• Maintains appropriate survivor privacy and chain of custody for all evidence collected, including Illinois State Police Evidence Collection Kit (ISPECK).
• Remains up to date on current regulatory and legislative guidelines related to treatment and documentation standards for sexual assault survivors.
• Educates survivors and their families to meet their emotional and healthcare needs to aid in the recovery process.
• Performs assigned work safely, adhering to established departmental safety rules and practices, reports to supervisor, in a timely manner, any unsafe activities, conditions, hazards, or safety violations that may cause injury to oneself, other employees, patients and/or visitors.
• Testifies in court as a fact witness and/or expert and assists other SANEs in preparing for court proceedings.
• Provides a learning atmosphere by sharing knowledge with coworkers; participates in orientation of new staff by providing content relevant to caring for sexual assault survivors.
• Supports continuous quality improvement efforts designed to enhance patient outcomes, increase patient satisfaction, and improve the overall care of sexual assault survivors
• Ensures professional growth and development by participating in and utilizing current evidence-based information and keeping current with standards in Forensic and SANE nursing practice.
• Maintains required medical and forensic continuing education requirements per current regulatory or legislative guidelines.
• Participates in goal setting, program development and evaluation of the regional and system-wide SANE programs.
• Attends monthly SANE meetings and participates in peer review.

Required:

• Bachelor of Science in Nursing (BSN) or Associate Degree Nursing (ADN) with commitment to obtain a BSN from an accredited program within three years of first day of employment in clinical nurse role OR Master’s degree from an accredited school/college of nursing and Advance Practice Registered Nurse (IL) license
• Current Illinois Licensure as a Registered Nurse in good standing
• BLS certification upon hire
• Completion of the IL SANE Clinical Training Program within 1 year of hireCompletion of an International Association of Forensic Nursing (IAFN) approved 40-hour didactic classCompletion of the IL SANE Clinical Training Log

Preferred:

• Adult/Adolescent SANE or Pediatric/Adolescent SANE
• Certified SANE-A or Certified SANE-P
• ACLS Certification
• TNCC or TNS
• PALS

Northwestern Medicine is an equal opportunity employer (disability, VETS) and does not discriminate in hiring or employment on the basis of age, sex, race, color, religion, national origin, gender identity, veteran status, disability, sexual orientation or any other protected status.

Background Check

Northwestern Medicine conducts a background check that includes criminal history on newly hired team members and, at times, internal transfers. If you are offered a position with us, you will be required to complete an authorization and disclosure form that gives Northwestern Medicine permission to run the background check.  Results are evaluated on a case-by-case basis, and we follow all local, state, and federal laws, including the Illinois Health Care Worker Background Check Act.

jobs.title: Prior Law Enforcement - Court Security Officer, Indianapolis, IN
jobs.description:
CSOs will provide armed security to courthouses under the USMS contract.

Essential Duties and Responsibilities: Includes the following and other duties may be assigned:

Perform entrance control: Enforce the District’s entry and identification system which includes operating security screening equipment to detect weapons, contraband, and prohibited items, checking items such as handbags, briefcases, computers, packages, baby carriages, wheelchairs, etc.

Perform roving patrol: Patrol court facilities and grounds of the facility in accordance with applicable post orders.

Perform stationary post assignments: Stand guard at stationary posts which include (but not limited to) monitoring closed-circuit television, duress alarm systems and other security equipment, courtrooms, judge chambers, and jury rooms.

Perform escort duties: When directed, provide armed escort services for judges, court personnel, jurors, and other designated individuals.

Perform garage parking and pedestrian control: Where applicable, direct traffic and control lights on court facility properties, as described in the post orders and/or standard operating procedures.

Enforce law and order: Enforce federal law while in the performance of assigned duties. This includes (but not limited to) detaining any person attempting to gain unauthorized access to Government property, or a court proceeding(s), or attempting to commit acts that imperil the safety and security of Government employees, property, and the public.

Prepare reports and records: Prepare various reports and records regarding contract performance issues, such as labor hours worked, accidents, fire, bomb threats, unusual incidents, or unlawful acts that occurred within the court facility area.

Court attendance: Responsible for securing unattended courtrooms, an inspection of courtrooms prior to a proceeding, testing of security devices, and other duties concerning security of the court area.

Preserve order: Responsible for providing security presence in the courtroom, enforcing federal law and judicial orders within the courtroom, enforcing local court rules regarding prohibited items, and providing protection to court proceedings as circumstances dictate.

Requirements

Education and/or Experience: High school diploma or general education degree (GED). At least three (3) calendar years of verifiable experience as a certified law enforcement officer or its military equivalency (Master-at-Arms, CGPD, Security Forces Specialist, etc.); all three (3) years must have occurred within the last seven (7) years. The experience must have included general arrest authority.

Language Skills: Must have the ability to read, write, speak, and understand English. Must possess the ability to understand, explain, interpret, and apply rules, regulations, directives, and procedures.

Certificates, Licenses, Registrations: Must have a valid driver's license from state of residency and a safe driving record for the past five years; Must receive clearance from the Department of Justice. Must have completed or graduated from certified Federal, state, county, local or military law enforcement training academy and able to provide certification as proof.

Other Qualifications: Must be at least 21 years of age; Ability to pass a pre-employment drug screen and criminal background check.

Physical Demands: Must meet medical standards as specified by the United States Marshal Service (USMS); The physical demands are based on the contract and must be met by an employee to successfully perform the essential functions of this job. Reasonable accommodations may be made to enable individuals with disabilities to perform the essential functions.

jobs.title: Clinical Research Nurse
jobs.description:
Purpose:

The Clinical Research Nurse is a specialized research professional working with and under the direction of the clinical Principal Investigator (PI). Assists with the execution of study-related activities of a Phase I clinical research study. Research nurses should primarily be concerned with the protection and care of research subjects. The primary role is to function as a licensed registered nurse engaged in the practice of care/assessments of the healthy volunteers and/or patient. Position includes disseminating information regarding new information for documentation, performance improvement and data source upgrades.

Responsibilities:

• Review protocols and informed consent forms for scheduled studies, identify and communicate potential issues to the appropriate personnel.
• Participate in nursing study related activities as required by protocol compliance with Corporate, divisional, and departmental SOP’s and external (CFR, ICH GCP) regulatory guidelines. Responsible for compliance with applicable Corporate and Divisional Policies and Procedures.
• Evaluate adverse events and manage safety reporting activities in a timely manner.
• Interact with the Principal Investigator and other study physicians, Recruiting/Screening, Data Systems, and other personnel in support of study-specific activities.
• Support quality and compliance improvement initiatives as appropriate.
• Participate in the recruitment and screening activities to ensure successful enrollment of volunteers into studies scheduled at the Phase 1 Unit. Interfaces with research participants to support efforts to determine eligibility and consenting of study participants according to protocol. Review and assess data collected. Serve as a resource person or act as a consultant within area of clinical expertise (R/S).
• Disburses investigational drug and provides teaching regarding administration, as necessary. Develops accurate source materials and ensures compliance from site staff. Ensures all protocol procedures are completed per study requirements (Unit).

Qualifications:

• For Recruiting & Screening: Minimum of a diploma from an accredited nursing school and 1-3 years work experience in a clinical research environment For Unit: Bachelor of Nursing or other Science degree preferred with 1-3 years of nursing experience in a hospital setting; and/or ER/ICU experience
• Nursing competency skills per scope of practice (i.e., performing vital signs, nursing assessments, performing ECG/EKG, administering injections, etc.)

jobs.title: Senior Data Architect (Snowflake)- Market Research
jobs.description:
ABOUT TRUELOGIC

At Truelogic we are a leading provider of nearshore staff augmentation services headquartered in New York. For over two decades, we’ve been delivering top-tier technology solutions to companies of all sizes, from innovative startups to industry leaders, helping them achieve their digital transformation goals.

Our team of 600+ highly skilled tech professionals, based in Latin America, drives digital disruption by partnering with U.S. companies on their most impactful projects. Whether collaborating with Fortune 500 giants or scaling startups, we deliver results that make a difference.

By applying for this position, you’re taking the first step in joining a dynamic team that values your expertise and aspirations. We aim to align your skills with opportunities that foster exceptional career growth and success while contributing to transformative projects that shape the future.




OUR CLIENT

This market research company provides trusted data, forecasts, benchmarks, and expert analysis across advertising, media, commerce, technology, healthcare, and financial services. It combines proprietary research with thousands of vetted sources to help organizations understand consumer behavior, anticipate market trends, validate strategies, and make faster, more confident and informed business decisions.



JOB SUMMARY

We are seeking a Senior Data Architect to design and optimize scalable data structures for complex analytical and business use cases. This role focuses on Snowflake architecture, data modeling, query performance, landing patterns, governance, and efficient data consumption across distributed environments. The ideal candidate will translate business requirements into accessible, high-performing datasets while partnering with Data Engineering, Data Science, Analytics, and business stakeholders. Success requires strong architectural judgment, advanced SQL expertise, and hands-on experience managing large-scale modern data platforms effectively.




RESPONSIBILITIES

 - Design scalable datasets optimized for analytics, reporting, and business consumption.

 - Review existing data structures and identify opportunities to improve query performance.

 - Define effective data landing patterns based on analytical, product, and operational requirements.

 - Optimize Snowflake architecture, including clustering, permissions, access patterns, governance, and performance.

 - Determine how large and complex datasets should be structured for efficient querying and consumption.

 - Design analytical solutions for data distributed across microservices and multiple source systems.

 - Collaborate with Data Engineering, Data Science, Analytics, and business stakeholders.

 - Establish data-modeling and architecture standards as the organization’s data ecosystem evolves.


QUALIFICATIONS AND JOB REQUIREMENTS

 - Senior-level experience in Data Architecture, Data Engineering, or Database Architecture.

 - Deep hands-on expertise with Snowflake.

 - Advanced knowledge of data modeling, dataset design, query optimization, and analytical architectures.

 - Experience designing scalable platforms for large or complex datasets.

 - Strong understanding of Snowflake clustering, permissions, performance optimization, and data governance.

 - Advanced SQL skills and strong relational database fundamentals.

 - Understanding of modern data pipelines and microservice-based architectures.

 - Ability to translate business and analytical requirements into efficient, accessible, and scalable data structures




WHAT WE OFFER

 - 100% Remote Work: Enjoy the freedom to work from the location that helps you thrive. All it takes is a laptop and a reliable internet connection.

 - Highly Competitive USD Pay: Earn an excellent, market-leading compensation in USD, that goes beyond typical market offerings.

 - Paid Time Off: We value your well-being. Our paid time off policies ensure you have the chance to unwind and recharge when needed.

 - Work with Autonomy: Enjoy the freedom to manage your time as long as the work gets done. Focus on results, not the clock.
